state_program_name: Assisted Living Program (Level 1, 2 or 3) licensed by MDH Office of Health Care Quality under HG §19-1801 et seq. and COMAR 10.07.14; Medicaid via the Home and Community-Based Options (Community Options) Waiver

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Assisted Living Program in Maryland. The program is licensed by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), under Md. Code, Health-General §19-1801 et seq. and COMAR 10.07.14. It is licensed for a stated number of beds and level of care (Level 1, 2 or 3), and **[AGENCY NAME]** serves residents only within that licensed level (COMAR 10.07.14.04, COMAR 10.07.14.05). Where the program participates in Medicaid, it also serves residents through the Home and Community-Based Options (Community Options) Waiver.

The manual has four goals:

1. **Protect residents.** It turns the licensing rules into everyday procedures for admission, service planning, medication management, incident reporting, restraints, resident rights, and abuse, neglect and financial exploitation.
2. **Support licensure and survey readiness.** Under COMAR 10.07.14.07, an applicant for initial licensure must submit the policies and procedures it will implement. OHCQ's on-site surveyor reviews them in Step Three of the licensing process. This manual is organized so those policies are in one place and ready at the facility.
3. **Give staff one reference.** Managers, alternate managers, the delegating nurse, medication technicians and direct care staff should be able to find what they must do, and who is responsible, without guessing.
4. **Support quality assurance.** The manual is the baseline for the written quality assurance plan and the periodic reviews required by COMAR 10.07.14.13.

This manual does not replace the law. If anything here conflicts with a statute, regulation or OHCQ directive, the law controls, and the manual must be corrected.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### Structure
The policy sections follow the order of OHCQ's policy list in the official application (Step Three, item 5, sub-items a through l), followed by the 4-week menu cycle (item 6) with the dietitian or nutritionist's written adequacy statement. Each policy states its purpose, who is responsible, the procedure, the records to keep and the regulatory basis. **Appendix A** is the crosswalk: it lists every official OHCQ item and shows which policy satisfies it.

### Who should use it
- **Assisted living manager and alternate manager:** the primary owners of the manual. They are responsible for adoption, updates and staff training.
- **Delegating nurse (RN):** uses the sections on assessment, service planning, delegation, medication management, restraints and clinical oversight.
- **Medication technicians and direct care staff:** use the sections that govern their daily tasks, resident rights, incident reporting, abuse and neglect reporting, and emergency procedures.
- **Governing body or owner:** adopts the manual and reviews it at least annually.

### Before first use: customize it
This manual is a template and is **not ready to use as written**. Before adoption:
1. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed field (address, license number, licensed beds and level, names and phone numbers of the manager, alternate manager and delegating nurse, local emergency contacts, pharmacy and dietitian details) with accurate information.
2. Adjust each policy to the program's actual size, licensed level, services, and whether it operates an Alzheimer's Special Care Unit, serves Medicaid waiver residents, transports residents, or permits smoking. Delete or mark "not applicable" any policy that does not apply, and record why.
3. Check each procedure against the current text of the cited rule. Some cross-referenced provisions, such as COMAR 10.27.11, COMAR 10.39.04, Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3, §19-1901, §19-347(g) and COMAR 10.07.21, were not independently read in preparing this template. Confirm them before adoption.

### Adoption
The governing body of **[AGENCY NAME]** must formally adopt the manual. Record the adoption date, the approving individuals or body and the version number on the adoption page. The adopted manual must be kept at the facility and available to staff and to OHCQ surveyors.

### Keeping it current
- Review the manual at least annually, and whenever a law, regulation or OHCQ directive changes, a survey or incident reveals a gap, or the program changes its licensed level, bed count, services or ownership.
- Keep a revision log with the date, what changed, who approved it and the effective date.
- Replace superseded pages promptly, and keep prior versions according to **[AGENCY NAME]**'s records policy.
- Where a change affects the operating license, follow the notice and approval steps in COMAR 10.07.14.08.

### Staff training
Every staff member must be trained on the policies relevant to their role. This applies at hire, when a policy changes and as part of ongoing training. Document who was trained, on what, when and by whom, and keep the proof in the personnel file (COMAR 10.07.14.19, COMAR 10.07.14.20). Staff must be able to find the manual at any time and must sign an acknowledgment that they have read the policies that apply to them.

### Using Appendix A
When preparing for the OHCQ on-site survey or a periodic self-audit, start with Appendix A. Confirm that each official item points to a current, adopted, customized policy and that the supporting records exist at the facility.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Governing statutes and rules

**Licensing and administration**
- **Md. Code, Health-General §19-1801 et seq.** — Statutory basis for licensing assisted living programs (definition, levels, penalties). COMAR 10.07.14 implements it.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.02** — Definitions (certified medication technician, delegation of nursing tasks, Resident Assessment Tool, incident, significant change, protective device). This manual uses these exact terms.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.04** — License required. The license is issued for a number of beds and a level of care and is displayed in a common-use area.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.05** — Levels of care (Level 1, 2 and 3). A resident may be served only within the licensed level.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.07** — Licensing procedure: application, business plan and 1-year budget, plan of correction, and provisional license. The program may not operate before a license or provisional license is issued, and an incomplete application may be closed after 180 days. This section requires submission of the policies and procedures to be implemented (§B(3)).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.08** — Changes that affect the operating license. Notify OHCQ immediately of application changes and report code citations within 7 days. Get OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising the level. Give 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds) of ownership change, relocation or closure. SDAT good standing is required.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.09** — Licensure standards waiver (written request citing the regulation and hardship; OHCQ decides within 45 days of a complete request).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.10** — Uniform Disclosure Statement. Give it free on request, include it in marketing materials, and file an amended statement within 30 days of a service change.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.12** — Compliance monitoring (annual on-site survey, which may extend to 18 months if there is no open plan of correction, complaint, civil money penalty or sanction).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.13** — Administration, including the written quality assurance plan, the 6-month manager and delegating nurse meeting, annual TB risk assessment and review of pharmacist findings.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.61** — Criminal penalties (operating without a license is a criminal offense; OHCQ gives 30 days' written notice to comply where residents were not harmed).

**Staffing, qualifications and training**
- **Md. Code, Health-General §19-1807** — Assisted living manager training (80-hour OHCQ-approved course with exam; 20 hours of continuing education every 2 years).
- **Md. Code, Health Occupations §9-3A-01** — Assisted living manager licensure (Board of Long-Term Care Administrators), required from July 1, 2026, with an interim provisional period.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.14** — Staffing plan (written plan covering scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day; awake overnight staff when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it; dated schedules kept on site for 18 months).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.15** — Assisted living manager.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.16–.17** — 80-Hour Assisted Living Manager Training Course.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.18** — Alternate assisted living manager.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.19** — Other staff qualifications and training.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.20** — Personnel records.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.21** — Delegating nurse.
- **Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901** — Criminal history records check.
- **COMAR 10.27.11** — Delegation of nursing functions (Board of Nursing).
- **COMAR 10.39.04** — Medication technician certification (Board of Nursing).

**Residents: admission, care and rights**
- **COMAR 10.07.14.22** — Preadmission requirements (Resident Assessment Tool within 30 days before admission; reviewed every 6 months).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.23** — Admission requirements, including non-discrimination and admission exclusions.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.27** — Resident agreement, financial content (at least 45 calendar days' notice of a rate increase).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.28** — Service plan.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.29** — Resident record.
- **Md. Code, Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3** — Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.30** — Services (meals, menus, personal care).
- **COMAR 10.15.03** — Food service facilities (applies to programs with a licensed capacity of 17 or more beds).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.31** — Medication management and administration.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.32** — Alzheimer's Special Care Unit (disclosure form and OHCQ written approval before operating).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.33** — Incident reports (within 24 hours of knowledge, with OHCQ notification for specified resident deaths).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.34** — Relocation and discharge.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.36** — Resident's rights (Resident Bill of Rights).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.37** — Abuse, neglect and financial exploitation.
- **Md. Code, Health-General §19-347(g)** — Immunity for good-faith reporters.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.38** — Restraints.
- **COMAR 10.07.21** — General hospice care programs (when a resident is under hospice care in the program).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.39** — Protection of a resident's personal funds.

**Physical plant, safety and emergency preparedness**
- **COMAR 10.07.14.43** — Water supply (resident hot water 100–120°F at the fixture).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.46** — Assist rails.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.47** — Emergency preparedness (NFPA 101 and local codes, extinguishers, Emergency Preparedness Packet, drills, evacuation, generator for 50+ residents).
- **COMAR 10.07.14.48** — Smoking.
- **COMAR 10.07.14.49–.51** — Common areas, resident rooms, bathrooms.

**Medicaid: Home and Community-Based Options (Community Options) Waiver** (applies if **[AGENCY NAME]** serves waiver residents)
- **COMAR 10.09.54.03** — Waiver eligibility and cost of care (room and board up to $420/month; the waiver pays services only).
- **COMAR 10.09.54.05** — Requirements for assisted living waiver providers.
- **COMAR 10.09.54.13** — Covered assisted living services.
- **COMAR 10.09.54.22** — HCBOW payment procedures.

Statutes and regulations change. Always confirm the current text before relying on any citation above. The COMAR 10.07.14 text referenced here is the version effective 4/28/2025.

### Official documents used to review this manual

1. **Application for Assisted Living Program License** (Step One: Initial License Application and Attachments; Step Two: Additional Documentation; Step Three: On-Site Survey). Issuer: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality, Assisted Living Team. No form number is printed. The file is named *APPLICATION_AL-License-04.13.2026-A.pdf* (10 pages) and is available at https://health.maryland.gov/ohcq/docs/Applications/APPLICATION_AL-License-04.13.2026-A.pdf. This is the only OHCQ document that lists the policies and procedures a new program must have. The list appears in **Step Three, "On-Site Survey," under the surveyor's record review, item 5 (Policies and procedures, sub-items a through l) and item 6 (menu cycle)**.
2. **COMAR 10.07.14.07B(3)** — the regulatory basis for the policy submission. It requires an applicant for initial licensure to submit "Policies and procedures to be implemented as designated in the application for licensure." The regulation does not list the individual policies, so the application's Step Three list serves as the checklist.

**How OHCQ reviews the manual.** The policies and procedures are not uploaded with Step One. The surveyor reviews them on site in Step Three, after OHCQ approves Steps One and Two. OHCQ states that the review "will include, but is not limited to" the listed documents, so keep the whole manual and its supporting records at the facility. If the survey finds deficiencies, the program receives a Statement of Deficiencies and has 10 business days to submit a Plan of Correction.

**Appendix A** maps every official item (Step Three, items 5a through 5l, and item 6, the 4-week menu cycle with the dietitian or nutritionist's written adequacy statement) to the specific policy in this manual that satisfies it. The OHCQ application is the authoritative source for the wording of each item.

**Related items outside the policy list.** The Resident Agreement (Step Two, item 6) and the Uniform Disclosure Statement (Step Two, item 5) are OHCQ forms or templates, and the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form (Step One, attachment 5) applies only if the program will operate such a unit. They are not policy-checklist items but are covered by this manual's policies. COMAR 10.07.14 also contains substantive requirements, such as medication management (.31), emergency preparedness (.47) and staffing (.14), that are not on OHCQ's policy list. They are addressed in this manual because the surveyor's review is not limited to the listed items.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training
This manual must be customized (all **[AGENCY NAME]** and bracketed placeholders completed), formally adopted by the governing body, kept current as laws, regulations and operations change, and taught to all staff. A manual that is generic, unadopted, outdated or unknown to staff will not demonstrate compliance, regardless of how complete the text is.

citations.requirement: Notify OHCQ immediately of application changes. Report code citations within 7 days. Get OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising the level. Give 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds) of ownership change, relocation or closure. SDAT good standing is required (§H).

citations.title: Licensure Standards Waiver
citations.requirement: Written waiver request citing the regulation and hardship. OHCQ decides within 45 days of a complete request.

citations.title: Uniform Disclosure Statement
citations.requirement: Complete the Uniform Disclosure Statement on the OHCQ form. Give it free to anyone who asks and include it in marketing materials. File an amended statement within 30 days of a service change.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: OHCQ conducts an annual on-site survey. The interval may extend to 18 months if there is no open plan of correction, complaint, civil money penalty or sanction.

citations.title: Administration
citations.requirement: Written quality assurance plan. Manager and delegating nurse meet every 6 months (§A(2)(b)). QA includes an annual TB risk assessment and review of pharmacist findings.

citations.title: Staffing Plan
citations.requirement: No numeric ratio. Written staffing plan covers scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day. Staff are present whenever a resident is in the building. Awake overnight staff are required when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it. Dated schedules are kept on site for 18 months. On-site nursing is required only when ordered.

citations.title: Assisted Living Manager
citations.requirement: Manager is age 21+ with a high school diploma and is licensed. Level 3 has added education and experience requirements. Manager needs a current background check, TB screening, MMR/varicella immunity, first aid and CPR.

citations.title: 80-Hour Assisted Living Manager Training Course
citations.requirement: Manager completes the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course and exam. Manager also completes 20 hours of CE every 2 years.

citations.title: Alternate Assisted Living Manager
citations.requirement: Alternate is age 21+ with 2 years of health-related experience and the .19B(1)–(7) staff qualifications. Alternate takes over when the manager is unavailable.

citations.title: Other Staff - Qualifications
citations.requirement: Age, TB/MMR/varicella evidence, background check within 30 calendar days before employment, and initial and annual training. Also first aid and CPR, delegating-nurse competency for personal care, relief staff, proof of training, and 6-hour/2-hour cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training.

citations.title: Personnel Records
citations.requirement: Lists the required contents of each personnel file. Includes the criminal history records check, TB/immunity evidence, flu and COVID-19 vaccine advised, licensure, training, and an OIG exclusion list check before hire.

citations.title: Delegating Nurse
citations.requirement: Signed RN agreement and Board of Nursing delegating nurse course. RN is on site to observe each resident at least every 45 days. RN is on call at all times (or an alternate is). RN has clinical oversight, issues nursing orders and reviews the manager's assessments.

citations.title: Preadmission Requirements
citations.requirement: Resident Assessment Tool completed within 30 days before admission. Assessment is reviewed every 6 months.

citations.title: Admission Requirements
citations.requirement: No discrimination by race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, physical disability or mental disability (§A). Do not admit anyone needing more than intermittent nursing care, stage 3 or 4 ulcer treatment, ventilator services, skilled monitoring with a fluctuating acute condition, or monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition (§B). Do not admit a person who is dangerous or at high risk that cannot be managed (§C). Hospice exception in §D.

citations.title: Resident Agreement - Financial Content
citations.requirement: Resident agreement states financial terms. At least 45 calendar days' notice of a rate increase.

citations.title: Service Plan
citations.requirement: Service plan within 30 calendar days of admission. Based on the Resident Assessment Tool and nursing assessment. Full assessment within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, and at least annually. Review every 6 months. Special care needs are addressed (falls, pressure ulcers, diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, catheter, ostomy, mental illness, behaviors). Resident and representative are invited to meetings.

citations.title: Resident Record
citations.requirement: Contents of the resident record. Delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours of readmission. Care notes at least weekly and on events. Record kept 5 years after discharge. Confidentiality and disposal follow HG Title 4, Subtitle 3.

citations.title: Services
citations.requirement: Three meals plus snacks daily. Menus written a week ahead, posted and kept 6 months. Dietitian or nutritionist reviews the 4-week menu before licensure and every 3 years. Personal care services are defined at §E.

citations.title: Medication Management and Administration
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff who administer medications complete the Board of Nursing medication technician course and are certified. Self-administration assessment with quarterly delegating-nurse reassessment. Regimen review within 14 calendar days of admission. Pharmacist on-site review every 6 months for residents on 9+ medications. Delegating nurse on-site review every 45 calendar days. Storage and documentation rules. Controlled substances are counted each shift, double-locked and destroyed on site.

citations.title: Alzheimer's Special Care Unit
citations.requirement: Submit the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form and get OHCQ's written approval before operating. Awake overnight staff are mandatory (§.14E(4)).

citations.title: Incident Reports
citations.requirement: Complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge. Reports are available on premises to OHCQ. Required content and notifications. Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program.

citations.title: Relocation and Discharge
citations.requirement: 5 calendar days' notice and consent for nonemergency relocation within the facility. 30 calendar days' notice before nonemergency discharge. Discharge planning and transfer documents. Emergency data sheet for acute transfer. Final statement, refunds and return of property within 30 calendar days. Attorney General may investigate funds abuse.

citations.title: Resident's Rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights with rights (a)–(aa). Give it to residents and representatives before or upon admission and post it or post where it is located. Confidentiality. Work only with consent and compensation. Adult day care attendance is voluntary and its policies are disclosed in the resident agreement.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect, and Financial Exploitation
citations.requirement: Written prohibition policies. Report within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, local Department of Human Services/APS, and the manager. Up to a $1,000 penalty if not reported within 3 days. Investigate and document on site. Post reporting signs. Do not knowingly employ individuals with harmful criminal history.

citations.title: Restraints
citations.requirement: No restraint for discipline or convenience. Physician order stating purpose, type and duration. No PRN restraint orders. Reposition and toilet at least every 2 hours. Renew every 7 calendar days. Delegating nurse trains staff. Bed rails may be restraints. Notify family or representative each time. No improper chemical restraint. Hospice coordination in §H.

citations.title: Protection of a Resident's Personal Funds
citations.requirement: May manage funds only on the resident's or agent's express written request. Interest-bearing account for $300 or more. Bond, letter of credit or net assets equal to the average monthly balance (State as obligee).

citations.title: Water Supply
citations.requirement: Resident hot water is 100–120°F at the fixture, with anti-scald or mixing valves.

citations.title: Assist Rails
citations.requirement: Assist rails on both sides of resident corridors for programs of 17 or more beds (.46B per the research checklist).

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness
citations.requirement: NFPA 101 and local codes. Extinguishers on each floor and in special hazard areas, serviced annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee. Staff trained in extinguisher use initially and annually. Emergency Preparedness Packet. 72-hour continuity. Tracking system and medical fact sheet. Plan reviewed annually. Evacuation sites and transportation agreements. Staff oriented within 24 hours. Quarterly fire drills on all shifts and semiannual disaster drills on all shifts, records kept 2 years. Generator for 50+ residents.

citations.title: Smoking
citations.requirement: Written smoking policy stating whether smoking is permitted. If permitted: fire-safe rules, designated areas, no smoking where oxygen or flammables are used or stored, and resident smoking assessment and annual reassessment in the service plan.

citations.title: Common Areas, Resident Rooms, Bathrooms
citations.requirement: Common space of 35 sq ft per bed. Public restrooms and COMAR 10.15.03 food service at 17+ beds. Maximum 2 residents per room, 80/120 sq ft. 1 toilet and sink per 4 residents and 1 tub/shower per 8.

citations.title: Criminal Penalties
citations.requirement: Operating without a license is a criminal offense. OHCQ gives 30 days' written notice to comply where residents were not harmed.

citations.title: Waiver eligibility and cost of care
citations.requirement: Waiver resident may be charged room and board of up to $420/month. The waiver pays services only (§D).

citations.title: Requirements for assisted living waiver providers
citations.requirement: At least 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime. Manager qualifications (physician, RN, LPN or 3 years of direct care). Alternate manager. Insurance if transporting residents. Cooperation with quarterly case-manager visits.

citations.title: Covered assisted living services
citations.requirement: Defines covered assisted living services under the waiver. Room and board are excluded.

citations.title: HCBOW payment procedures
citations.requirement: Payment is the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate.

citations.title: Delegation of nursing functions (Board of Nursing)
citations.requirement: Medications administered by unlicensed staff must comply with this chapter (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.31C and K). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Medication technician certification (Board of Nursing)
citations.requirement: Medication technician training and certification are documented in the personnel file (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.31B). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act
citations.requirement: Resident medical records are released and disposed of as permitted by this subtitle (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.29H). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Criminal history records check
citations.requirement: Basis for the staff criminal history records check documented under COMAR 10.07.14.20I. Text not independently read.

citations.title: Immunity for good-faith reporters
citations.requirement: Civil immunity for a person who reports abuse, neglect or exploitation in good faith (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.37F). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Food service facilities
citations.requirement: Applies to programs with a licensed capacity of 17 or more beds. Smaller programs follow the basic food safety rules in COMAR 10.07.14.48 and any directive from OHCQ or local jurisdiction.

citations.title: General hospice care programs
citations.requirement: Hospice and the assisted living program each comply with their own chapter when a resident is under hospice care in the program (COMAR 10.07.14.38H). Text not independently read.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All levels of care (Level 1, 2 and 3); governing body, Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, and to set the qualifications, licensure, training and duties of the Assisted Living Manager (ALM) and the Alternate ALM. This ensures a qualified person is always in charge of the program.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is licensed as an assisted living program under Md. Code, Health-General §19-1801 et seq. and COMAR 10.07.14. The governing body is legally responsible for the program. It appoints a qualified ALM and a qualified Alternate ALM, and gives them the authority and resources to run the program in compliance with the law. The ALM is at least 21 years old and has a high school diploma. From July 1, 2026 the ALM must hold a current assisted living manager license from the Maryland State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators. The ALM completes the OHCQ-approved 80-hour assisted living manager course and passes the exam, then completes 20 hours of continuing education every 2 years. A program that fails to meet the manager training requirement may be penalized up to $10,000. If the program is licensed at Level 3, the ALM also meets the added education and experience requirements in COMAR 10.07.14.15. The ALM has a current criminal background check, TB screening, evidence of MMR and varicella immunity, and current first aid and CPR certification. The Alternate ALM is at least 21 years old, has 2 years of health-related experience, meets the staff qualifications in COMAR 10.07.14.19B(1)-(7), and takes over the ALM's duties whenever the ALM is unavailable. The Board license verification for the ALM is posted in the program. Any interim or provisional manager status allowed by Health Occupations §9-3A-01 (up to 90 days, extendable up to 30 days) is used only when needed and is tracked by date.

definitions.definition: The owner(s), board or members of [AGENCY NAME] who hold legal responsibility for the program and appoint the ALM.
The licensed individual responsible for the day-to-day operation of the program and for compliance with COMAR 10.07.14.
The designated person who meets the alternate manager qualifications and assumes the ALM's duties when the ALM is unavailable.
The Maryland State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators, which licenses assisted living managers.
The Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality, which licenses and surveys assisted living programs.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written organizational chart that shows the governing body, the ALM, the Alternate ALM, the delegating nurse, and direct care, dietary, housekeeping and maintenance staff. The ALM keeps the chart current and available to staff and surveyors.

Before appointing an ALM, the governing body verifies and documents that the candidate is at least 21 years old, has a high school diploma, and holds (or is eligible for, as applicable by date) the Board license.
For a Level 3 program, the governing body verifies and documents that the candidate meets the added Level 3 education and experience requirements in COMAR 10.07.14.15 before the appointment is made.
The governing body verifies and files proof of completion of the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course and passing exam, and records the completion date.

The ALM completes a criminal history records check, TB screening, MMR and varicella immunity evidence, and current first aid and CPR before assuming duties. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] keeps this evidence in the ALM's personnel file (see STF-02, STF-04 and STF-05).
The ALM tracks the 2-year continuing education cycle (20 hours), keeps certificates in the personnel file, and reports the cycle end date to the governing body 90 days before it closes.

From July 1, 2026 the ALM keeps the Board license current. The ALM posts the Board license verification in a common-use area next to the facility license, and the governing body checks the expiration date every quarter.

If an ALM vacancy occurs, the governing body names an interim manager at once. Any interim or provisional period under Health Occupations §9-3A-01 is tracked by start date, limited to 90 days with at most a 30-day extension, and the governing body tells OHCQ of the change under GOV-02.

The governing body designates an Alternate ALM in writing. It verifies that this person is at least 21 years old, has 2 years of health-related experience, and meets the COMAR 10.07.14.19B(1)-(7) qualifications, and files the verification in the personnel file.

The ALM posts a written schedule of who is in charge each shift and lists how to reach the ALM and the Alternate ALM at all times. When the ALM is absent or unreachable, the Alternate ALM assumes authority and documents that in the shift log.

The ALM manages day-to-day operations, including admissions, staffing, resident rights, record-keeping, emergency preparedness, QA, and communication with OHCQ. The ALM reports to the governing body at least quarterly on census, incidents, grievances, staffing, finances, survey results and open corrective actions.
The governing body reviews the ALM's and Alternate ALM's qualifications every year and records the review in governing body minutes.
The governing body supplies enough budget, staff and supplies to operate within the licensed bed count and level of care (see GOV-02 and STF-01). It documents these decisions in minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints and verifies the ALM and Alternate ALM; funds the program; reviews quarterly reports; keeps the program in compliance with Health-General §19-1801 et seq. and COMAR 10.07.14.
Holds the Board license; completes the 80-hour course and 20 hours of CE every 2 years; posts the license verification; runs the program daily; reports to the governing body.
Meets the alternate qualifications and assumes authority whenever the ALM is unavailable; documents the coverage.
Maintains qualification and credential records and expiration tracking for the ALM and Alternate ALM.

documentation: Organizational chart and governing body minutes
ALM and Alternate ALM qualification verification checklists
Board license verification (posted) and copy in file
80-hour course certificate and exam result; CE certificates
Background check, TB screening, MMR/varicella evidence, first aid and CPR for ALM
Alternate ALM designation and coverage log
Quarterly ALM report to the governing body

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Changes Affecting the License and OHCQ Surveys
policies.applies_to: All levels of care (Level 1, 2 and 3); governing body, ALM and Alternate ALM
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a valid OHCQ license, within its licensed bed count and level of care. It also sets out how the program reports changes to OHCQ, requests waivers, and handles OHCQ surveys.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not accept residents or operate as an assisted living program until OHCQ has issued a license or provisional license (COMAR 10.07.14.07). Operating without a license is a criminal offense under COMAR 10.07.14.61; where residents have not been harmed, OHCQ gives 30 days' written notice to comply. The license names a bed count and a level of care (Level 1 low, Level 2 moderate, Level 3 high). [AGENCY NAME] never exceeds either one, and serves a resident only within the licensed level (COMAR 10.07.14.05). The license is displayed in a common-use area (COMAR 10.07.14.04). The program notifies OHCQ immediately of changes to the information in its application, and reports any code citation to OHCQ within 7 days. It obtains OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising its level of care. It gives OHCQ 60 days' notice of an ownership change, relocation or closure (49 or fewer beds). It stays in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) (COMAR 10.07.14.08). The program cooperates fully with OHCQ surveys, which occur at least annually, with the interval extendable to 18 months when there is no open plan of correction, complaint, civil money penalty or sanction (COMAR 10.07.14.12).

definitions.definition: A license OHCQ may issue while an applicant completes requirements; the program may not operate until a license or provisional license is issued.
Level 1 (low), Level 2 (moderate) or Level 3 (high), as stated on the license.
The program's written response to OHCQ survey findings, stating how and when each deficiency will be corrected.
OHCQ's written approval to vary from a specific COMAR 10.07.14 requirement due to hardship.
Current status of the business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, including annual report filing.

procedures: The governing body submits the OHCQ application, with the business plan, 1-year budget and all required attachments. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] answers OHCQ requests promptly so the application is not closed as incomplete; OHCQ may close an incomplete application after 180 days.
No resident is admitted, and no assisted living services are advertised as available, until the license or provisional license is in hand. The ALM files a copy in the licensure binder.
On receipt of the license, the ALM posts it in a common-use area that residents and visitors can see. The ALM checks the posting at least monthly and after any renovation.

The ALM keeps a census report showing licensed beds, occupied beds and each resident's care level. Admissions are accepted only if the bed count and the licensed level of care will not be exceeded (see ADM-01, ADM-02 and ADM-05).
If the program wants to add beds or raise its level of care, the ALM submits the request to OHCQ and waits for written approval before accepting any resident into the new beds or at the higher level.
The ALM notifies OHCQ immediately of any change to information in the application (for example, owner, ALM, address, phone, or services). The notice is written, dated, and filed.
The ALM reports every code citation received from a fire marshal, health department or other code authority to OHCQ within 7 days. The ALM logs the citation date and the report date.

At least 60 days before an ownership change, relocation or closure (49 or fewer beds), the governing body gives OHCQ written notice. It begins resident notification and transfer planning under ADM-07 and ADM-08.

The ALM confirms SDAT good standing every year after the annual report is filed and files the certificate or confirmation. A lapse is reported to the governing body the same day and corrected at once.

To request a licensure standards waiver, the ALM submits a written request that cites the specific COMAR 10.07.14 provision and describes the hardship. OHCQ decides within 45 days of a complete request. The program does not rely on the waiver until it is approved in writing.

During an OHCQ survey, the ALM or Alternate ALM greets the surveyors, provides a private workspace, and supplies requested records, the policy manual and staff access without delay. The ALM or designee takes notes and keeps copies of anything given to the surveyors.

After the exit conference, the ALM sends the written plan of correction to OHCQ by the due date on the statement of deficiencies. The ALM assigns each correction to a named person with a completion date and verifies completion.
Survey findings, plans of correction and completion evidence are reported to the governing body at its next meeting and reviewed in the QA process (GOV-04).
If OHCQ gives written notice of any operating-without-license concern, the governing body responds in writing within the 30-day notice period and documents each corrective step.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains and maintains the license; approves bed or level changes and OHCQ notices; maintains SDAT good standing.
Posts the license; enforces bed and level limits; makes OHCQ reports on time; leads survey response and plans of correction.
Handles survey and OHCQ contacts whenever the ALM is unavailable.
Checks census and licensed level before each admission.

documentation: OHCQ license, provisional license and application file
Census and level-of-care log
Copies of notices to OHCQ with dates, and code citation report log
Waiver requests and OHCQ decisions
SDAT good standing confirmation
Survey reports, statements of deficiencies, plans of correction and completion evidence

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: All programs; all policies, procedures, forms and posted documents
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME]'s written policies are current, approved, available to staff, and ready for an OHCQ on-site survey, and that required documents (such as the Uniform Disclosure Statement and the emergency plan) are updated on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps all written policies and procedures required for licensure current, approved by the governing body, and available to staff and to the OHCQ surveyor on site (COMAR 10.07.14.07). The emergency and disaster plan is reviewed at least annually (COMAR 10.07.14.47). The Uniform Disclosure Statement is amended and filed with OHCQ within 30 days of any change in services (COMAR 10.07.14.10). Every policy carries an ID, effective date, version number and approver. A version log and staff acknowledgment are kept for each revision.

definitions.definition: A policy, procedure, form or plan that has an ID, version, effective date and approval, and that may be changed only through this policy.
A register that shows each revision, its date, the reason, the approver and the staff acknowledgment date.
The OHCQ form describing the program's services and fees, which the program gives free to anyone who asks and includes in marketing materials.

procedures: The ALM keeps a master policy index that lists each policy ID, title, version, effective date, last review date, next review date and policy owner.
The governing body approves each new or revised policy in writing before it takes effect and records the approval in its minutes.
The ALM keeps one master copy of the manual on site, in a binder or secure electronic file, that is available to all staff at all times and to OHCQ surveyors on request.
The ALM reviews every policy at least annually and records the review date and any changes in the version log, even if no changes were made.
The ALM reviews the emergency and disaster plan (SAF-05) at least once every 12 months and documents the date, reviewers and changes.
The ALM triggers an interim review when a regulation changes, after a survey citation, after a serious incident, after a QA finding (GOV-04), or when a service, fee or practice changes.

When services change, the ALM updates the Uniform Disclosure Statement on the current OHCQ form and files the amended statement with OHCQ within 30 days of the change. The ALM also updates the resident agreement and marketing materials (RR-04).
The ALM keeps a copy of the current Uniform Disclosure Statement at the front desk and gives it free to any person who requests it.
The ALM issues each revised policy with its new version number and date. Staff sign an acknowledgment within 14 days of issue, and the ALM trains staff on material changes.
The ALM removes superseded copies from use and files them in an archive marked 'superseded'. As an agency standard, [AGENCY NAME] keeps superseded versions for at least 6 years.
The ALM checks forms, posted notices and handouts against the current policy every 6 months so that no outdated forms stay in use.
At the start of each OHCQ survey, the ALM provides the master manual, the index and the version log to the surveyor.

responsibilities.duty: Approves policies and revisions; reviews the policy review schedule.
Owns the master manual, index and version log; schedules reviews; files the amended Uniform Disclosure Statement within 30 days; ensures the annual emergency plan review.

responsibilities.role: Policy owners (delegating nurse, dietary lead, maintenance lead)
responsibilities.duty: Draft revisions to their policies and assist with annual review.
Read and sign acknowledgment of new or revised policies and follow current versions.

documentation: Master policy index and version log
Governing body approval minutes
Staff acknowledgment sheets for each revision
Annual emergency plan review record
Amended Uniform Disclosure Statement and OHCQ filing proof
Archive of superseded versions

policies.title: Quality Assurance Plan and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: All levels of care; governing body, ALM, delegating nurse and all staff
policies.purpose: To establish a written quality assurance (QA) plan that checks on resident care, safety and compliance, finds problems early, and records corrective action.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(l), p. 10 — Quality Assurance Plan. [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written quality assurance plan as required by COMAR 10.07.14.13. The ALM and the delegating nurse meet at least every 6 months, and the meeting is documented (COMAR 10.07.14.13A(2)(b)). The QA plan includes an annual TB risk assessment and a review of the findings from the pharmacist's reviews (COMAR 10.07.14.13 and .31). It also reviews incidents, resident grievances and OHCQ survey findings, and documents corrective action for each problem found. Results are reported to the governing body. The QA plan is also available to the OHCQ surveyor, who conducts an on-site survey at least annually (COMAR 10.07.14.12).

definitions.definition: The written plan describing what [AGENCY NAME] monitors, how often, who is responsible, and how problems are corrected.
The registered nurse who delegates nursing tasks to staff and monitors residents under a signed agreement with the program.
An annual evaluation of the program's risk of TB exposure that guides staff and resident TB screening.
Written results of the pharmacist's on-site medication reviews for residents on 9 or more medications, performed every 6 months.

procedures: The ALM writes the QA plan, which lists each measure monitored, the data source, the frequency, the person responsible and the target. The governing body approves the plan and reviews it every year.

The ALM and the delegating nurse meet at least every 6 months. They discuss resident care, medication management, delegation, staff competency and any resident changes of condition. The ALM writes minutes that both sign, with the date and attendees.
The ALM keeps a QA calendar that lists the 6-month meeting dates, the annual TB risk assessment date and the quarterly QA reviews, so no item is missed.

Each year, the ALM and the delegating nurse complete a TB risk assessment of the program, document it and use the result to set the TB screening approach for staff and residents (see STF-04 and SAF-07).

The delegating nurse gives the ALM a summary of the pharmacist's findings after each review (every 6 months for residents on 9 or more medications). The ALM and the nurse assign each recommendation to a person for action. They record whether it was accepted or declined, the date and the reason, and the prescriber's response when relevant (see HLT-01).

The delegating nurse's on-site observations (at least every 45 calendar days under COMAR 10.07.14.31) and medication errors are summarized in the QA review. Trends are noted and corrective steps assigned.

Each quarter, the ALM reviews all incident and accident reports (SAF-02), including falls, elopement, injury, medication errors and hospital transfers. The ALM identifies patterns by resident, time, place and staff and records actions taken.
Each quarter, the ALM reviews all complaints and grievances (RR-02): the number, type, time to resolution and the resident's satisfaction with the outcome.

After each OHCQ survey, the ALM reviews every finding, whether or not it was cited, together with the plan of correction. The ALM verifies that each correction was completed and re-checks it 30 and 90 days later.
For each problem found, the ALM writes a corrective action that states what will change, who is responsible and the due date. The ALM follows up until it is complete and records the result.

The ALM reports QA results (meeting minutes, TB assessment, pharmacist findings, incident and grievance trends, survey status and open actions) to the governing body at least quarterly. The governing body records its review and any direction in its minutes.
The ALM shares QA findings that affect staff practice with staff in meetings or in-service training (see STF-03). Staff are not disciplined for reporting concerns in good faith.
The ALM keeps all QA records and makes them available to OHCQ on request. The QA plan is reviewed and revised at least annually under GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the QA plan; reviews quarterly QA reports; provides resources for corrective action.
Writes and runs the QA plan; leads the 6-month meeting with the delegating nurse; tracks corrective actions.
Participates in the 6-month meeting; reports on pharmacist findings, medication practice and clinical trends; helps carry out the TB risk assessment.
Report incidents, concerns and near-misses promptly and take part in corrective actions.

documentation: Written QA plan and annual review record
Minutes of the ALM and delegating nurse meetings every 6 months
Annual TB risk assessment
Pharmacist review findings and response log
Quarterly incident, grievance and survey trend reports
Corrective action log and follow-up verification
Governing body minutes showing QA review

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, ALM, billing and admissions staff, and all employees and contractors
policies.purpose: To prevent and detect fraud, waste, abuse and billing errors, to keep [AGENCY NAME] from employing or contracting with excluded persons, and to make sure Medicaid and private charges follow the rules.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills accurately and honestly and follows all laws on Medicaid billing. We do not submit false claims (False Claims Act, 31 USC 3729-3733). We do not offer, pay, solicit or receive anything of value for referrals (Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 USC 1320a-7b). We do not employ or contract with a person excluded from federal health care programs (42 USC 1320a-7). Medicaid payment to the program is the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate (COMAR 10.09.54.22). The Medicaid waiver pays for covered services only; room and board are excluded from covered assisted living services (COMAR 10.09.54.13) and are billed to the resident, and for a waiver resident may not exceed $420 per month (COMAR 10.09.54.03D). Every employee is checked against the OIG exclusion list before hire, and the check is documented in the personnel file (COMAR 10.07.14.20). Sanctions and civil money penalties for violating licensure rules are set out in COMAR 10.07.14 and may be imposed by OHCQ.

definitions.definition: A request for payment that the provider knows, or should know, is false or inflated, including billing for services not provided or not documented.
Anything of value offered or accepted to induce or reward referrals of Medicaid-covered business.
The federal List of Excluded Individuals/Entities maintained by the HHS Office of Inspector General.
The amount [AGENCY NAME] regularly charges the general public for the same service.
The person designated by the governing body to oversee this policy; unless otherwise named, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].

procedures: The governing body names a compliance officer in writing. Staff are told who that person is and how to reach them, including an anonymous reporting option.

At orientation and annually, every employee receives training on this policy, including the False Claims Act, Anti-Kickback rules, exclusion rules, accurate documentation and how to report concerns. Attendance is recorded (see STF-03).

Before an offer of employment is final, the HR designee checks the candidate against the OIG exclusion list and prints or saves the result with the date. The result is filed in the personnel file (COMAR 10.07.14.20). A candidate found on the list is not hired.

As an agency standard, the HR designee re-checks all employees and contractors against the OIG exclusion list every month and records the date. An employee found excluded is removed from duty immediately, and the compliance officer consults counsel.
Billing staff bill Medicaid only for covered services that were actually delivered and documented in the resident's record and service plan (see ADM-04 and REC-02).
Billing staff set each Medicaid claim at the lesser of the program's customary charge or the Medicaid rate. The ALM confirms the customary charge on the current rate sheet each year.

Billing staff never bill Medicaid for room and board. Room and board are billed to the resident or representative under the resident agreement (RR-04). For a waiver resident, the charge is never more than $420 per month.

The ALM does not accept or pay any money, gift or favor in exchange for resident referrals, and does not split fees with a referral source. Proposed marketing or referral arrangements are reviewed by the compliance officer before they begin.
Each quarter, the compliance officer samples claims or invoices against attendance, service plans and records for accuracy, and writes up the results in a short audit memo.

If an overpayment or billing error is found, the compliance officer stops further billing of that type, corrects the claims and refunds the overpayment promptly, as required by law. The event and the correction are documented.

Staff may report a compliance concern to the compliance officer, the ALM or the governing body, or anonymously. Nobody is retaliated against for reporting in good faith. Retaliation is grounds for discipline up to termination.

The compliance officer investigates each report promptly, documents the findings and corrective actions, and reports to the governing body. Suspected fraud may be reported to the appropriate state or federal agency, as the compliance officer and counsel determine.
The compliance officer reports the results of audits, exclusion checks and investigations to the governing body at least quarterly, and the results feed into the QA plan (GOV-04).
Billing and compliance records are kept as long as required by law and not less than 6 years as an agency standard.

responsibilities.duty: Names the compliance officer; reviews quarterly compliance reports; sets the tone for honest billing.
Runs training, audits, investigations and reports; reviews referral and marketing arrangements.
Runs and files the OIG exclusion checks before hire and monthly thereafter.
Bill the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate for covered services only; exclude room and board from claims.
Document accurately, complete training and report concerns.

documentation: Compliance officer designation and training attendance records
OIG exclusion check results (pre-hire and monthly)
Rate sheet, customary charge record and claim audit memos
Overpayment correction and refund records
Compliance reports, investigations and governing body minutes

policies.title: Medicaid Community Options Waiver Participation
policies.applies_to: Programs enrolled as Medicaid assisted living providers under the Home and Community-Based Options (Community Options) Waiver
policies.purpose: To state how [AGENCY NAME] meets the Maryland Medicaid requirements for assisted living providers in the Community Options Waiver, including staffing, manager qualifications, case manager cooperation, billing and room and board charges.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] participates in the Medicaid Home and Community-Based Options (Community Options) Waiver and follows COMAR 10.09.54. We keep at least 1 staff member for every 8 residents in the daytime (COMAR 10.09.54.05). The manager is a physician, RN, LPN or has 3 years of direct care experience, and we name an alternate manager. We carry insurance if we transport residents. We cooperate with the waiver case manager's quarterly visits. The waiver pays for covered assisted living services only (COMAR 10.09.54.13), not room and board. A waiver resident may be charged room and board of up to $420 per month (COMAR 10.09.54.03D), and our rate sheets reflect that limit. Payment is the lesser of our customary charge or the Medicaid rate (COMAR 10.09.54.22). Each waiver resident's services are provided in line with the person-centered service plan and the home and community-based settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c), including the resident's choice, privacy, dignity and community access.

definitions.definition: The Maryland Home and Community-Based Options Waiver, run by the Maryland Medicaid Office of Long Term Services and Supports, that pays for assisted living services for eligible residents.
The waiver case manager who monitors the resident's plan of care and visits at least quarterly.
Assisted living services paid by the waiver (COMAR 10.09.54.13); room and board are not covered.
The Maryland Medicaid provider enrollment and revalidation system.
The Maryland Medicaid long-term services and supports system used for waiver authorizations and billing.

procedures: Before enrolling, the governing body confirms that the entity is in good standing with SDAT and holds a current OHCQ assisted living license (GOV-02). It then applies through MPRIME, which requires an SDAT number in good standing. The ALM files the approval and the Medicaid provider number.

The governing body keeps the enrollment current through MPRIME revalidation. The ALM sets a calendar reminder 90 days before each revalidation date and updates SDAT and OHCQ information whenever it changes.

The ALM verifies and documents that the manager meets the waiver requirement (physician, RN, LPN or 3 years of direct care) in addition to the OHCQ requirements in GOV-01, and that a qualified alternate manager is named.

The ALM schedules staff so there is at least 1 staff member for every 8 residents on each daytime shift. The ALM calculates the ratio from the census at the start of every shift, and documents it on the staffing schedule (see STF-01). Any shortfall is corrected at once by calling in staff.
If the program transports residents, the ALM carries insurance that covers resident transport. The ALM files the certificate and confirms the coverage each renewal (see DL-04).

When a waiver applicant is referred through the Maryland Access Point (844-627-5465) or the Medicaid program, the ALM follows pre-admission screening, assessment and service plan steps (ADM-01, ADM-03, ADM-04) and confirms that the applicant's care needs fit the licensed level and the waiver level (Level II or Level III).

The ALM tells the waiver resident, before or at admission, what the waiver pays for and what the resident must pay. The resident agreement states room and board charges that do not exceed $420 per month for a waiver resident (see RR-04).
Billing staff bill only services that are covered under COMAR 10.09.54.13. They never bill Medicaid for room and board, and they never charge a waiver resident extra for waiver-covered services.

Billing staff use the MDH rate transmittal in effect on the date of service (PT 04-25: $90.74 per day for Level II and $114.51 per day for Level III, without medical day care). Before each billing cycle, the ALM verifies with the Office of Long Term Services and Supports (410-767-1739) that these rates are still current, because rates are subject to change.
Billing is submitted in LTSSMaryland, which has been the billing system from October 1, 2026. Billing staff direct system questions to the LTSSMaryland helpdesk at 1-855-463-5877.
Payment is the lesser of the program's customary charge or the Medicaid rate. Billing staff compare the two each time the rate or the customary charge changes.

The ALM welcomes the case manager's quarterly visits, makes the resident's record, service plan and staff available, and keeps a log of each visit date and any follow-up. The ALM completes any follow-up the case manager requests within the time they set.
The ALM tells the case manager promptly of any significant change in the resident's condition, hospitalization, incident or proposed discharge, in line with HLT-04 and ADM-08.

The ALM honors the resident's rights in the waiver setting: the resident may have visitors, privacy, control of their schedule and personal belongings, and access to the community. Any limit must be justified in the person-centered plan and agreed to by the resident or representative.
The QA plan (GOV-04) includes a quarterly check of the 1-to-8 daytime ratio, case manager visits, billing accuracy and room and board charges for waiver residents.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains enrollment, SDAT good standing and insurance; approves rate sheets and the waiver participation plan.
Meets and verifies the manager qualifications; ensures the daytime 1-to-8 ratio; coordinates with case managers; oversees billing and room and board limits.
Meets the alternate qualifications and covers the manager's duties when the ALM is unavailable.
Bill the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate for covered services only; keep the rate sheet current.

responsibilities.role: Delegating nurse and direct care staff
responsibilities.duty: Deliver and document services in line with the service plan; report changes in condition.

documentation: Medicaid provider enrollment and MPRIME approval and revalidation records
Manager and alternate manager qualification verification
Daily staffing schedules showing the daytime 1-to-8 ratio
Transport insurance certificate (if transporting residents)
Case manager quarterly visit log
Rate transmittal in use and rate verification record
Resident agreements showing room and board charges of $420 per month or less for waiver residents
Claims, remittances and audit memos

policies.title: Resident Bill of Rights, Responsibilities and Resident Representative
policies.applies_to: All residents, resident representatives, and all staff of [AGENCY NAME] (Maryland Assisted Living Program, Level 1, 2 or 3, including residents funded through the Community Options Waiver)
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident knows, and is able to exercise, the rights set out in the Maryland Resident Bill of Rights, and to describe how a resident may use a resident representative.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] recognizes and protects each right in the Resident Bill of Rights in COMAR 10.07.14.36, rights (a) through (aa). Before or upon admission, the Assisted Living Manager (or designee) gives the complete Bill of Rights to the resident and to the resident's representative, if any. The Bill of Rights is posted in a place accessible to residents and visitors. If it is not posted in full, a sign is posted that tells residents where a copy is kept. Residents' personal and health information is kept confidential. A resident works for the program only if the resident consents and is compensated. Attendance at adult day care, if offered by [AGENCY NAME], is voluntary, and the adult day care policies are disclosed in the resident agreement. A resident may choose a resident representative and the program works with that person as the resident directs. [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate, and it provides accommodations for disability consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act. For residents receiving Home and Community-Based Services, the program supports the rights and setting expectations of 42 CFR 441.301(c), including privacy, dignity, choice and community integration. Residents may exercise these rights without fear of retaliation.

definitions.definition: The list of resident rights (a) through (aa) in COMAR 10.07.14.36 that must be given to every resident and representative.

A person the resident chooses, or who is legally authorized, to receive information or act for the resident to the extent the resident or the law allows. The representative's role and limits are recorded in writing.
Displayed in a common area where residents and visitors can read it, or, if not displayed in full, a posted notice states where the full document is kept and available.

procedures: Before or upon admission, the Assisted Living Manager gives the resident, and the representative if one has been named, a complete copy of the Resident Bill of Rights (rights (a) through (aa)).

The Manager or designee reviews the rights with the resident in plain language, in the resident's preferred language, and in a format the resident can use (large print, interpreter, reading aloud). See RR-08.

The resident, or the representative if the resident cannot, signs and dates an acknowledgment of receipt. The acknowledgment is filed in the resident record. If the resident refuses to sign, staff write a note with the date and reason and file it.

The Manager posts the Bill of Rights in a common area in a spot accessible to residents and visitors. If a notice that says where the Bill of Rights is kept is posted instead, the full text is kept at that location and is available at all times without asking.
The Manager checks the posting monthly with the environmental rounds checklist and replaces any missing or damaged copy within 1 business day.

At admission and any time a resident asks, staff identify whether the resident wants a resident representative. A representative is recorded in the resident record with name, relationship, contact information, the legal document (if any), and the scope of the representative's role.

Staff respect the resident's own choices. A representative acts only to the extent the resident wishes or the law provides. A representative does not override the resident's decisions where the resident has capacity.
The resident's right to confidentiality is observed in every setting. Staff discuss resident information only with persons the resident has authorized, or as the law allows. See RR-07.

No resident is required to perform work for [AGENCY NAME]. Any work a resident does is voluntary, consented to by the resident, documented in the service plan, and paid at an agreed rate. The Manager approves such arrangements in writing.
If the program offers adult day care, the Manager makes it clear in the resident agreement that attendance is voluntary and discloses the adult day care policies. See DL-05.

Staff are trained on resident rights during orientation and at least annually. The training covers dignity, choice, privacy, confidentiality and the non-retaliation rule. Attendance is documented. See STF-03.

Staff who see or learn of a rights violation tell the Manager the same day. The Manager looks into it, takes corrective action, and documents the outcome. Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation follow SAF-01.

Residents are told at admission and again at the resident council or in meetings, at least annually, about their responsibilities: following the resident agreement, respecting other residents' rights and property, paying agreed charges on time, telling staff about changes in health, and following posted safety rules (for example, smoking and evacuation).
Residents who disagree with a decision may use the complaint procedure in RR-02. The Manager tells residents they may also contact OHCQ and the Ombudsman. See RR-03.
The Manager reviews rights complaints and the Bill of Rights acknowledgments in the quality assurance review each quarter. See GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy and provides the resources needed to protect resident rights.
Gives and posts the Bill of Rights, obtains acknowledgments, supervises staff practice, and investigates alleged violations.
Reinforces residents' rights in care delivery, including consent and privacy during care.
Honor residents' rights, protect confidentiality, report violations, and never retaliate.
Follow the agreement and house safety rules, treat others with respect, pay agreed charges, and tell staff about changes in health or needs.
Acts within the scope the resident or the law has set and puts the resident's wishes first.

documentation: Signed Bill of Rights acknowledgment in the resident record
Resident representative designation and scope, with any legal document
Posting checklist showing monthly verification of the posted Bill of Rights
Consent and payment record for any resident work arrangement
Rights training attendance records
Rights violation investigation notes and corrective action

policies.title: Complaint and Grievance Procedure
policies.applies_to: All residents, resident representatives, family members and staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To give residents and their representatives a clear, written way to raise complaints and grievances, and to make sure each one is received, investigated, answered and documented without retaliation.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(g), p. 10 — Complaint and Grievance Procedure. Every resident and representative may make a complaint or grievance, orally or in writing, about any aspect of care, services, staff, other residents, charges or the program, without fear of retaliation. [AGENCY NAME] receives, investigates, responds to and documents each complaint following the written procedure below. Residents and representatives are given the contact information for the OHCQ Assisted Living Team, (410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005, and for the Long-Term Care Ombudsman (see RR-03). Using the internal procedure is never required before a resident contacts OHCQ, the Ombudsman or any other agency. [AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate, and does not allow staff to retaliate, against a person who makes a complaint. Any complaint that alleges abuse, neglect or financial exploitation is handled under SAF-01, including the 24-hour reports required by COMAR 10.07.14.37. Complaint and grievance trends are reviewed in the quality assurance plan required by COMAR 10.07.14.13.

definitions.definition: Any expression of dissatisfaction or concern from a resident, representative or family member, whether oral or written.
A complaint that is not resolved at the time it is raised, or that involves a serious matter, and so is logged and investigated formally.
Any adverse action, threat, or change in treatment taken because a person made or supported a complaint.

procedures: At admission, the Assisted Living Manager gives each resident and representative a written copy of this procedure. It includes the name of the staff person who takes complaints ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [PHONE]), the OHCQ Assisted Living Team contact ((410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005), and the Ombudsman contact ([OMBUDSMAN PHONE]).
The same contact information is posted in a common area next to the Resident Bill of Rights.

Any staff member who hears a complaint listens, treats it seriously, and records it the same shift on the Complaint/Grievance Log form. Staff help residents who need assistance putting a complaint in writing.
Staff tell the Manager about every complaint no later than the next business day. Complaints involving resident safety, abuse, neglect or exploitation are reported to the Manager immediately.

If an allegation involves abuse, neglect or financial exploitation, the Manager follows SAF-01 immediately, including reports within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, and the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services.
The Manager acknowledges each complaint to the resident or representative, orally or in writing, within 2 business days.

The Manager investigates. This includes interviewing the person who complained, any staff or residents involved, and reviewing records. The Manager takes immediate steps to protect the resident when there is a risk to health or safety.

The Manager sends a written response to the person who complained within 14 calendar days. If the investigation needs more time, the Manager tells the person why and when to expect the answer. The response states the findings, any action taken or planned, and how to take the matter further.

If the person is not satisfied, the Manager offers a meeting with the Manager and, if the resident wishes, a person of the resident's choice. The Governing Body representative reviews any unresolved grievance within 30 calendar days.
The Manager reminds the resident and representative at each response that they may contact OHCQ and the Ombudsman at any time, and that the program will not retaliate.

No staff member may discourage, delay or discipline a person for raising a complaint. Any suspected retaliation is investigated by the Manager and corrected. Staff who retaliate are subject to discipline, up to termination.
Anonymous complaints are logged and investigated as far as the information allows.
If OHCQ or another agency contacts [AGENCY NAME] about a complaint, the Manager cooperates fully and gives the agency access to the information it requests. See GOV-02.
The Manager keeps the Complaint/Grievance Log and enters each complaint's date, nature, investigation, outcome and response date. The Manager summarizes the log at least quarterly.
The summary, with the number, type and resolution of complaints, is reviewed in the quality assurance meeting, and corrective actions are assigned. See GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Receives, investigates, responds to and logs complaints; protects against retaliation; reports abuse allegations.
Performs these duties when the Manager is unavailable.
Helps investigate complaints about care, medications or health services.
Accept and record complaints, report them promptly, help residents who need assistance, and never retaliate.
Reviews unresolved grievances and complaint trends, and requires corrective action.

documentation: Complaint/Grievance Log
Complaint intake forms and investigation notes
Written responses to complainants
Resident-record entry if the complaint involves care
Quarterly complaint summary and quality assurance minutes
Acknowledgment that the procedure was given at admission

policies.title: Long-Term Care Ombudsman and Agency Access
policies.applies_to: All residents, staff and visitors of [AGENCY NAME]; Ombudsman and OHCQ representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can reach the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and State agencies, and that Ombudsman and OHCQ representatives have the access to residents and records that the law allows.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and representatives of OHCQ to enter the program and to have access to residents, and to records as permitted by law and the resident's consent where consent is required. Residents may contact the Ombudsman or OHCQ at any time and may speak with them in private. Contact information for the Ombudsman, the local area agency on aging and the OHCQ Assisted Living Team is posted where residents and visitors can see it. It is also given to residents and representatives at admission. [AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate against any resident, representative or staff member who contacts or cooperates with these agencies. Allegations of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation are reported within 24 hours to the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, together with law enforcement, OHCQ and the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services, as set out in SAF-01 and COMAR 10.07.14.37. The Ombudsman's role under 42 USC 3058g and 45 CFR 1324 Subpart A is respected in all dealings.

definitions.definition: A State-designated advocate who receives and works to resolve complaints made by or for residents of long-term care facilities, including assisted living.
The local agency that serves older adults in the program's county and, in Maryland, may act as the local Ombudsman contact.
The Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality, which licenses and surveys assisted living programs.

procedures: The Manager posts, next to the Resident Bill of Rights, a notice with the Ombudsman name and phone ([OMBUDSMAN PHONE]), the local area agency on aging ([AREA AGENCY ON AGING PHONE]), and the OHCQ Assisted Living Team ((410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005).
At admission, the Manager gives the same contact information in writing to the resident and representative and explains it. A signed acknowledgment is filed in the resident record.

Residents may call or write the Ombudsman or OHCQ at any time. Staff help a resident place a call or send a letter on request, and do not listen in, read, delay or screen the resident's communication.

When an Ombudsman or OHCQ representative arrives, any staff member on duty notifies the Manager or Alternate Manager at once. Staff do not make the representative wait without good reason or refuse entry.
The Manager asks to see identification, writes the person's name, agency and time of arrival in the visitor log, and then offers access to residents and a private space for interviews.
Residents decide whether to speak with the representative. Staff do not require a resident to meet or to refuse to meet.

Access to a resident's record is given to the Ombudsman or OHCQ as permitted by law. Where the resident's consent is needed, the representative obtains it from the resident or the resident's legal representative. The Manager documents what was shared. See RR-07.
The Manager gives the surveyor or Ombudsman any information or records requested within the time asked, and keeps a copy of what was given.
Staff must not coach residents, discourage contact, or retaliate. A staff member who retaliates is subject to discipline up to termination.
If an Ombudsman or OHCQ finding or complaint is received, the Manager investigates, responds in writing, and takes corrective action. See RR-02 and GOV-02.

Any allegation of abuse, neglect or financial exploitation is reported within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, the local Department of Human Services/APS, and the Manager. See SAF-01.
Staff are trained at orientation and annually on residents' right to contact the Ombudsman and OHCQ and on the access procedure above. Attendance is documented.

The Manager checks the posting monthly and replaces it within 1 business day if it is missing or out of date. The contact list is also reviewed every 6 months and whenever agencies change their contact details.

responsibilities.duty: Posts and updates contact information, receives Ombudsman and OHCQ visitors, gives access, and responds to findings.
Provides access and receives visitors when the Manager is away.
Tell the Manager at once when a visitor arrives, help residents contact agencies, and never obstruct or retaliate.
Makes sure the program cooperates with oversight agencies.

documentation: Posted contact notice and monthly posting check
Admission acknowledgment of agency contact information
Visitor log entries for Ombudsman and OHCQ visits
Record of any resident information shared and the consent obtained
Responses and corrective action plans to agency findings
Staff training attendance records

policies.title: Resident Agreement, Uniform Disclosure Statement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Residents, representatives, prospective residents, and the Manager, business office and admission staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident has a written agreement stating all services and charges, that anyone who asks can get the Uniform Disclosure Statement free, and that increases, deposits, refunds and final statements are handled as Maryland requires.
policies.policy: Each resident, or the resident's representative, signs a written resident agreement before or at admission. [AGENCY NAME] uses the OHCQ sample resident agreement, which states the nonfinancial terms and the financial terms. The financial terms (COMAR 10.07.14.27) state each charge, what it covers, and when it is due. [AGENCY NAME] gives at least 45 calendar days' written notice of a rate increase. The program completes the Uniform Disclosure Statement on the OHCQ form (COMAR 10.07.14.10), gives it free to anyone who asks, includes it in marketing materials, and files an amended statement with OHCQ within 30 calendar days of a change in services.
