policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, delegating nurse, certified medication technicians, direct care staff, and all residents who receive hospice or home health services in the program
policies.purpose: To make sure a resident who chooses hospice or home health care while living at [AGENCY NAME] receives coordinated, safe and dignified care. The hospice or home health agency and the assisted living program each stay responsible for their own duties under Maryland law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] supports a resident's choice to receive hospice or home health services in the program. COMAR 10.07.14.23 limits who may be admitted for nursing needs, but it contains a hospice exception in section D. [AGENCY NAME] uses that exception only as far as the section allows and only while the program can safely meet the resident's needs with the hospice's help. When a resident is under hospice care in the program, the hospice follows COMAR 10.07.21 and [AGENCY NAME] follows COMAR 10.07.14. Neither one takes over the other's legal duties. Before hospice or home health services begin, [AGENCY NAME] signs a written coordination agreement with the provider. The agreement sets out who does what, and the resident's service plan reflects it (COMAR 10.07.14.28). Any restraint or protective device order for a hospice resident is coordinated with the hospice under COMAR 10.07.14.38H. Hospice and home health do not change the resident's rights under RR-01 or the resident's right to choose a provider.

definitions.definition: A general hospice care program that provides palliative and comfort-focused care to a resident with a terminal illness and is regulated under COMAR 10.07.21.
A licensed agency that provides skilled nursing, therapy or aide services to a resident in the program under a practitioner's order.
A written agreement between [AGENCY NAME] and the hospice or home health provider that assigns responsibilities for care, communication, medications, emergencies and death.
The written plan required by COMAR 10.07.14.28, based on the Resident Assessment Tool and the nursing assessment.
The registered nurse who delegates nursing tasks and oversees the program's nursing functions, as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02.

procedures: When a resident, representative or practitioner asks for hospice or home health, the Assisted Living Manager tells the delegating nurse the same day and records the request in the resident record.

The resident (or representative) chooses the hospice or home health provider. Staff may give a list of Medicare- and Medicaid-certified providers, but staff do not steer the choice. The choice is documented.

The delegating nurse reviews the resident's needs against COMAR 10.07.14.23 and the hospice exception in §D and the program's retention limits in ADM-05. The delegating nurse reports to the Manager whether the program can safely meet the resident's needs with the added support. The Manager decides and records the reasons.

Before services start, the Manager signs a written coordination agreement with the provider. It covers: contact names and 24-hour phone numbers, visit schedules, who gives which care, medication ordering and delivery, equipment and supplies, who staff call first in a crisis, and what happens at the time of death.

The hospice or home health provider gives [AGENCY NAME] its plan of care. The delegating nurse completes a reassessment with the Resident Assessment Tool within 48 hours after the change in condition or start of hospice. The service plan is updated and shared with the provider (COMAR 10.07.14.28).

The shared service plan states which tasks belong to hospice or home health staff and which to program staff. It also states the resident's comfort, spiritual and cultural wishes and the advance directive status (RR-06).

The delegating nurse and the hospice or home health nurse talk at the start of services and after any significant change. Each contact is recorded in the resident record with date, names and decisions.

Medications ordered by the hospice are added to the medication record and handled under HLT-01 and HLT-02. Comfort-kit or controlled medications are counted on receipt, locked and reconciled. Unused medications are disposed of per HLT-01 after a death or discontinuation.

Direct care staff report to the delegating nurse any new symptom, pain, refusal of care, fall or other change. The nurse tells the hospice or home health nurse and the practitioner as the agreement directs (HLT-04).

If a restraint or protective device is considered for a hospice resident, the delegating nurse contacts the hospice and the practitioner before use. The order, its purpose, type and duration, and the monitoring plan are coordinated under COMAR 10.07.14.38H and follow SAF-04. No restraint is used for convenience or discipline.
Visits by hospice staff, volunteers, clergy and family are welcomed at any reasonable time. Staff give privacy during visits and for personal care.
Hospice and home health staff who enter the program wear identification and follow the program's infection control, confidentiality and visitor rules (SAF-07, RR-07, SAF-09).

The Manager and delegating nurse review the shared service plan at least every 6 months, and sooner after any significant change. If needs rise above what the program can safely meet, the Manager follows ADM-05 and ADM-08, with the hospice and the resident or representative involved.
At death, staff follow HLT-09 and the coordination agreement. The hospice is called as the agreement directs.
The Manager reviews every coordination agreement during annual policy review (GOV-03). Problems with a provider are discussed with that provider and raised in QA (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether the program can serve the resident, signs coordination agreements, keeps copies, and acts on provider problems.
Assesses the resident, communicates with the hospice or home health nurse, updates the service plan, and trains staff on the shared plan and any restraint coordination.
Give medications as ordered and delegated, record them, and report changes to the delegating nurse.
Give personal care per the service plan, watch for changes, offer comfort, and report concerns right away.
Chooses providers, takes part in service plan meetings, and states care preferences.

policies.title: Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, Alternate Manager, delegating nurse, all direct care and administrative staff
policies.purpose: To make sure a resident's death is handled with dignity, that the right people and OHCQ are notified on time, and that the resident's property, final statement and record are handled as Maryland rules require.
policies.policy: When a resident dies, [AGENCY NAME] treats the resident and family with respect and follows the resident's advance directive and wishes (RR-06). Staff notify the resident's representative and the resident's practitioner promptly. [AGENCY NAME] notifies OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death that results from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns, or any injury incurred at the program, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.33. The Manager completes an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge of that event. [AGENCY NAME] returns the resident's property and gives the final statement and any refund due within 30 calendar days (COMAR 10.07.14.32). The resident record is kept for 5 years after discharge, which includes death (COMAR 10.07.14.29).

definitions.definition: An event as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02 that must be reported on an incident report.
The person the resident has named, or who is legally authorized, to act for the resident (RR-01).
The written account of charges, payments, deposits and personal funds, with any refund owed.

procedures: A staff member who finds a resident not breathing or unresponsive starts emergency response per the resident's advance directive or code status on file (RR-06) and calls 911 unless a valid do-not-resuscitate order is on file. Staff stay with the resident and tell the Manager and the delegating nurse at once.

If the death was expected, for example a hospice resident, staff call the hospice as directed by the coordination agreement (HLT-08). If the hospice is not involved, staff call the practitioner or the authority who can pronounce death. If the death is unexpected or suspicious, staff call 911 and follow law enforcement and emergency personnel direction.

Staff leave the resident's room and belongings undisturbed when the death is unexpected or suspicious or involves an injury or incident, until released by law enforcement or investigators. Otherwise they give privacy and respect in handling the body.

The Manager or the delegating nurse notifies the resident's representative and family contacts as soon as possible, preferably by phone and in person when appropriate. Notification is recorded with the date, time and person reached.
The Manager or the delegating nurse notifies the resident's attending practitioner promptly. The practitioner is told about the circumstances and any medications given that day.

The Manager decides the same day whether the death falls within COMAR 10.07.14.33 (abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns, or any injury incurred at the program). If so, the Manager notifies OHCQ at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005 within 24 hours and confirms the notice in writing by fax to (410) 402-8211.

For any death in the 24-hour category, the Manager also completes an incident report within 24 hours of learning of it (SAF-02). If abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, the Manager also follows SAF-01 at once. If elopement is involved, see SAF-03.

Staff keep the resident's medications and controlled-substance records secure. The delegating nurse documents the last medications given. Medications are held and later disposed of per HLT-01. Nothing is given to the family unless the program's policy and the law allow it.

Staff release the body only to a funeral home or authorized person named by the representative, or as directed by law enforcement or hospice. The release is documented with the time, the name of the receiving party and the staff member present.

If no representative or family can be found, the Manager follows the State's requirements for an unclaimed resident, including any approval needed for burial or cremation. The Manager documents every attempt to find family.

The Manager protects the resident's personal property by listing it with two staff present, and stores it securely. Property is released only to the representative, the personal representative of the estate or another person legally entitled to it, against a signed receipt (RR-05).

Within 30 calendar days of the death, the Manager returns the resident's property, issues a final statement, and refunds any deposit or prepaid fees due and any personal funds held (COMAR 10.07.14.32; RR-04, RR-05). Charges after the date of death are not made beyond what the resident agreement and law allow.
The Manager stops any Medicaid or other billing as of the date of death and notifies the Community Options case manager or other payer as required (GOV-06, GOV-05).

Within 7 days, the delegating nurse and Manager complete the record with a death note: date and time, circumstances, who was notified and when, and who received the body and property. The Manager checks that every required entry is present (REC-01).
The record is kept for 5 years after discharge. Confidentiality and disposal follow Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.29 (RR-07, REC-01).

The Manager tells residents and staff about the death with sensitivity and respects privacy. Staff and residents are offered support, and a memorial or chance to say goodbye may be arranged with the family's permission.
The Manager reviews every death at the next QA meeting (GOV-04) to identify any care or safety issue.

responsibilities.duty: Directs the response, notifies OHCQ when required, completes the incident report, returns property, issues the final statement and refund within 30 calendar days, and ensures the record is complete.
Notifies the practitioner and hospice, documents the clinical circumstances and medications, and secures medications.
Start emergency response when required, stay with the resident, protect privacy and property, and report to the Manager immediately.
Prepare the final statement, stop billing and process refunds.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Policy
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers, the Assisted Living Manager, the Alternate Manager and the governing body; residents, representatives and visitors are informed of how to report
policies.purpose: To protect each resident from abuse, neglect and financial exploitation, and to make sure any suspicion is reported, investigated and documented as COMAR 10.07.14.37 requires.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(i) — Abuse, Neglect, and Financial Exploitation Policy, and COMAR 10.07.14.37. [AGENCY NAME] prohibits abuse, neglect and financial exploitation of any resident by any person. Anyone who knows of or suspects it reports it right away. A report must reach law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or the area agency on aging, the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services, and the Assisted Living Manager within 24 hours. A penalty of up to $1,000 applies if a required report is not made within 3 days. [AGENCY NAME] investigates every allegation on site and documents it, and posts reporting signs where residents and visitors can see them. [AGENCY NAME] does not knowingly employ individuals with a criminal history that would harm residents (STF-02). A person who reports in good faith has civil immunity under Md. Code, Health-General §19-347(g), which COMAR 10.07.14.37F cross-references. [AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate against any resident, family member or employee who reports. [AGENCY NAME] manages a resident's money only as COMAR 10.07.14.39 allows (RR-05).

definitions.definition: Any willful act or threat that causes physical harm, pain, emotional distress, sexual contact without consent, or unreasonable confinement of a resident.
Failure to give a resident the care, supervision, food, hygiene, medication or services needed for health and safety.
Improper or unauthorized use of a resident's money, property or assets, including coercing gifts, taking funds or misusing a power of attorney.
A belief, based on what a person has seen, heard or learned, that abuse, neglect or exploitation may have happened. Proof is not required before reporting.
An event as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02 that must be recorded on an incident report (SAF-02).

procedures: At hire and at least annually, every employee, contractor and volunteer is trained on this policy, the signs of abuse, neglect and exploitation, and how and where to report (STF-03). Attendance is documented.

The Manager posts reporting signs in a public area and near each resident bulletin board. The signs list the phone numbers for law enforcement, OHCQ ((410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005), the Ombudsman or area agency on aging [PHONE], local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services [PHONE], and the Manager [PHONE].

Any person who sees or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation protects the resident from harm first. They call 911 if the resident is in danger or needs medical care, and then tell the Manager or Alternate Manager at once. If the Manager is the person suspected, they report directly to the outside agencies and the governing body [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT].

The staff member who has knowledge or suspicion does not wait for the Manager before reporting. Staff may report directly to any of the five parties. The Manager makes sure all five have received a report.

Within 24 hours of knowledge, the Manager (or designee) reports to each of: (a) law enforcement [LOCAL POLICE PHONE]; (b) OHCQ; (c) the Ombudsman or the area agency on aging [PHONE]; (d) the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services [PHONE]; and (e) the Manager, if the report was made by someone else. The reporter and time of each call are recorded.
A report not made to the required parties within 3 days can lead to a penalty of up to $1,000. The Manager keeps a checklist for each report so that no party is missed and the dates are provable.

Staff separate the alleged abuser from the resident at once. An employee who is accused is removed from resident contact during the investigation. Contractors, family members and visitors are restricted from access as needed.

The Manager arranges any medical care and emotional support the resident needs, and notifies the resident's representative and practitioner as soon as possible, unless the representative is the suspected person (HLT-04).

The Manager completes an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge (SAF-02) and starts an on-site investigation. The Manager collects written statements from the resident, witnesses and staff involved. The Manager secures evidence and reviews records, schedules, medication and financial records, and security footage if it exists.

The Manager cooperates fully with OHCQ, law enforcement, Adult Protective Services and the Ombudsman, gives them access to residents, staff and records, and does not interfere with any outside investigation.

The Manager completes a written investigation summary stating the facts, the finding, the actions taken to protect the resident, and any corrective action. The summary is filed in the investigation file, not in the resident record alone. A note about the event and the resident's condition is placed in the resident record (REC-02).

If financial exploitation is alleged, the Manager reviews the resident's funds account, ledgers and receipts (RR-05). The Manager follows COMAR 10.07.14.39, under which funds are managed only on the resident's or agent's express written request. The Manager informs the authorities that the Attorney General may investigate abuse of residents' funds (COMAR 10.07.14.34).

Substantiated misconduct leads to discipline up to and including termination, and a report to the licensing board or registry as the law requires (STF-02, STF-06). An employee found to have abused a resident is not rehired.

No one is punished or retaliated against for reporting in good faith. Retaliation is itself grounds for discipline. Staff are told that good-faith reporters have civil immunity under Md. Code, Health-General §19-347(g).
Backgrounds are checked before hire and at the intervals required, and no one is knowingly hired with a harmful criminal history (STF-02).
The Manager tells the resident and representative of the outcome of the investigation and the steps taken to keep the resident safe, within confidentiality limits (RR-07).
The Manager reports all allegations, findings and trends to the governing body and reviews them at each QA meeting (GOV-04). The policy is reviewed at least annually (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy, receives reports of allegations and findings, and investigates any allegation involving the Manager.
Posts signs, makes or confirms the 24-hour reports, protects the resident, investigates and documents on site, and takes corrective action.
Carries out the Manager's duties when the Manager is absent.
Protect residents, report suspicion immediately, cooperate with investigations, and never retaliate.
Assesses injuries, documents findings and gives clinical input to the investigation.

Incident report completed within 24 hours of knowledge
Witness statements and investigation summary
Corrective action and discipline record
Staff training attendance records
Photo or copy of the posted reporting signs and posting location
Notice to the resident and representative of the outcome

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
policies.applies_to: All staff; the Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager review and file reports
policies.purpose: To make sure every incident or accident involving a resident is recorded, reported to the right people on time, kept on site for OHCQ, and used to improve safety.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] completes an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge of any incident, using the meaning of "incident" in COMAR 10.07.14.02. Incident reports are kept on the premises and made available to OHCQ on request (COMAR 10.07.14.33). When a resident dies from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program, [AGENCY NAME] also notifies OHCQ within 24 hours (HLT-09). [AGENCY NAME] reviews incidents in its QA program to find causes and prevent a repeat (GOV-04).

definitions.definition: An event defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02 that affects or could affect a resident's health, safety or rights, such as a fall, injury, medication error, elopement, abuse allegation, or an unexpected change that requires emergency care.
An unplanned event, such as a fall or burn, that results in or could result in injury.
The time at which any staff member sees, is told of, or otherwise learns of the incident.
A change in the resident's condition as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02 that triggers reassessment (ADM-03).

procedures: The staff member who sees or learns of an incident first makes sure the resident is safe and gets first aid or emergency care, calling 911 when needed (HLT-04).
The staff member tells the Manager (or the Alternate Manager on duty) and the delegating nurse as soon as the resident is safe, and no later than the end of the shift.

The staff member who saw or learned of the incident completes the incident report form before the end of the shift. The report is finished within 24 hours of knowledge at the latest. It records: resident name; date, time and place; what happened in factual terms; who was involved or witnessed; injuries and condition; care given; who was notified and when; and the staff member's name and signature.

The delegating nurse examines the resident after any injury or suspected injury, documents findings, and tells the practitioner as needed (HLT-04). Fall and skin injuries are also handled under HLT-06 and HLT-07.
The Manager notifies the resident's representative and practitioner promptly. The time and name of the person reached are written on the report.
The Manager reviews each report within one working day and signs it. The Manager checks that the facts are complete and that required notifications were made.

If the incident involves suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Manager makes the 24-hour reports to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, and the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services under SAF-01.

If a resident dies from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program, the Manager notifies OHCQ at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005 within 24 hours, following HLT-09.
If the incident is an elopement or missing resident, the Manager follows SAF-03. If it involves a restraint or protective device, see SAF-04. If it involves a medication error, see HLT-01 and HLT-02.

The Manager decides what immediate action will prevent a recurrence, such as a change in the service plan, extra supervision, equipment, or staff retraining, and records it on the report. The delegating nurse reassesses the resident if there is a significant change (ADM-03, ADM-04).

Reports are filed on the premises in a secure incident file, ordered by date and kept apart from or cross-referenced to the resident record. They are available to OHCQ surveyors on request. A brief note of the incident is entered in the resident record (REC-02).
The Manager keeps a monthly incident log with the type, time, place, and staff on duty. The log is used to spot trends.
The Manager presents incident totals, trends and corrective actions at each QA meeting (GOV-04) and reports summaries to the governing body.
Reports are kept for at least the period set out in REC-01 and are protected under RR-07. Staff do not discuss incidents with persons not involved in the resident's care except as the law allows.
New staff are trained on this policy during orientation, and all staff are retrained annually (STF-03).

responsibilities.role: Staff who sees or learns of the incident
responsibilities.duty: Protect the resident, report to the Manager and complete the incident report within 24 hours.
Assesses the resident, informs the practitioner and reassesses when there is a significant change.
Reviews every report, makes required notifications including to OHCQ, orders corrective action and files reports on site.
Reviews incident trends and ensures corrective action is taken.

documentation: Incident report form with times and notifications
Incident file kept on the premises and available to OHCQ
Monthly incident log and trend summary
OHCQ notification record (when applicable)
Resident record note and updated service plan if needed
QA minutes showing incident review

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff, with added duties for staff in the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit and for overnight staff
policies.purpose: To prevent a resident from leaving the program unsafely and to ensure a fast, organized search and response if a resident is missing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] knows where each resident is, assesses each resident's risk of wandering or elopement before and after admission, and puts protections in place that respect resident rights. A staff member is present whenever a resident is in the building or is expected back. If the program operates an Alzheimer's Special Care Unit, it has awake overnight staff at all times, as COMAR 10.07.14.32 (§.14E(4)) requires. [AGENCY NAME] uses the resident tracking system that is part of its emergency preparedness plan under COMAR 10.07.14.47 (SAF-05). Any security device such as a door alarm must be consistent with NFPA 101 and local fire codes and must never block emergency exit. If a resident dies after an elopement, [AGENCY NAME] notifies OHCQ within 24 hours and completes an incident report within 24 hours, as COMAR 10.07.14.33 requires.

definitions.definition: A resident leaving the building or grounds without staff knowledge, or without the supervision the resident's service plan requires, when leaving puts the resident at risk.
A resident whose location is unknown and who is not where the resident is expected to be.
Aimless or repetitive movement that can lead a resident into danger or out of a safe area.
The sign-in/sign-out and census method used to know where each resident is, including during emergencies (COMAR 10.07.14.47).

procedures: During pre-admission screening and the Resident Assessment Tool, the delegating nurse documents any history of wandering, exit-seeking, confusion or elopement and rates the risk (ADM-01, ADM-03). The risk and the plan to reduce it go into the service plan (ADM-04).

A current photo and description (height, weight, hair, clothing worn, identifying marks) of each resident at risk is kept in the resident record and an elopement binder at [LOCATION]. It is updated at least every 6 months, at each service plan review, and after any change in appearance.

A staff member is assigned to be present at the program whenever a resident is in the building or is expected back. Staffing patterns are set under STF-01 so that this holds on every shift, including nights, weekends and outings.
If the program operates an Alzheimer's Special Care Unit, staff on the unit are awake all night, every night. The Manager checks the overnight schedule weekly (HLT-05).

Residents sign out and in under the resident tracking system when leaving and returning with family or staff. The shift supervisor checks the sign-out sheet at each shift change. At-risk residents are checked at intervals set in the service plan, and the check is documented.

Door alarms, exit chimes or other devices may be used only if consistent with NFPA 101 and local codes. Staff test them weekly and record the test. No exit is blocked or locked in a way that prevents emergency egress (SAF-06).

Staff who see a resident trying to leave stay calm, redirect the resident and tell the shift supervisor. They document the event and report it to the delegating nurse, who considers a change to the service plan.

When a resident is found missing or staff suspect elopement, the staff member immediately tells the shift supervisor and calls out the alert code [ALERT CODE] so that all staff on duty help. The census is taken at once and the last-seen time and place are recorded.

Within the first 15 minutes, staff search the room, bathrooms, common areas, closets, stairwells, basement, outdoor areas and parking lot. They check vehicles and neighboring areas near the building. The search is led by the shift supervisor, and one staff member stays with the other residents.

If the resident is not found within 15 minutes, or at once if the resident is high-risk, in danger, or the weather is severe, the shift supervisor calls 911 and gives the resident's description and photo. The supervisor then calls the Manager, the delegating nurse and the resident's representative.

The Manager goes to the program (or directs the Alternate Manager) and takes command of the search. The Manager coordinates with law enforcement, supplies the photo and medical information, and keeps staff searching until the resident is found.

When the resident is found, staff give first aid and call 911 if there is any injury or concern. The delegating nurse examines the resident, and the practitioner and representative are notified (HLT-04).
The Manager completes an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge (SAF-02), including the timeline, search steps and how the resident left.

If a resident dies because of an elopement or wandering, or is injured or burned, the Manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours at (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005 (HLT-09). If neglect is suspected, the Manager also reports under SAF-01.
After each event, the Manager and delegating nurse review the cause, change the service plan, fix any door or alarm failure, and retrain staff. The event is reviewed at QA (GOV-04).
Elopement drills are held at least twice a year on all shifts, and staff training on this policy is given at orientation and annually (STF-03). Drill dates and findings are recorded.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure staff are present and awake as required, commands a search, notifies OHCQ when required, and leads the review.
Assesses elopement risk, updates service plans and examines a resident who has been found.
Starts the alert and search, calls 911 as required, keeps the census and checks the sign-out record.
Know where residents are, redirect exit-seeking residents, take part in searches and document.

documentation: Elopement risk assessment and service plan entries
Current resident photo and description file
Sign-in/sign-out and tracking records
Door alarm test log
Missing resident search timeline and incident report
OHCQ notification record, when applicable
Drill and training records

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse, certified medication technicians, all direct care staff, and contracted practitioners
policies.purpose: To make sure no resident is restrained for discipline or convenience, and that any restraint used is ordered, monitored, time-limited and used safely, as COMAR 10.07.14.38 requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not use any restraint, physical or chemical, for discipline or convenience. A restraint may be used only under a physician's order that states the purpose, the type and the duration. A PRN (as-needed) restraint order is not accepted. A restrained resident is repositioned and offered toileting at least every 2 hours. Each order is renewed every 7 calendar days or the restraint stops. Bed rails may be restraints and are handled under this policy. The delegating nurse trains staff on restraint use. The resident's family or representative is notified each time a restraint is used. [AGENCY NAME] does not use any improper chemical restraint. For a resident under hospice care, [AGENCY NAME] coordinates restraint orders with the hospice (COMAR 10.07.14.38H; HLT-08). The meaning of "protective device" is the one given in COMAR 10.07.14.02.

definitions.definition: Any physical device, material or equipment, or any drug used as a restriction, that limits a resident's freedom of movement or normal access to the body and that the resident cannot easily remove.
A medication used to control behavior or restrict movement for discipline or staff convenience, and not to treat a diagnosed condition.
A device as defined in COMAR 10.07.14.02. Any device that restricts a resident's movement is reviewed under this policy.
An as-needed order. A PRN order for a restraint is not accepted.
Use of a restraint to make care easier for staff or to make up for too few staff, not to meet a resident's medical symptoms.

procedures: Staff never use a restraint, seclusion, or a threat of either, to punish a resident or for staff convenience. A staff member who is asked to do so refuses and reports it to the Manager. Misuse is reported under SAF-01 as abuse.

Before any restraint is considered, the delegating nurse assesses the resident and the cause of the behavior or safety risk, and documents less restrictive options tried: toileting schedule, pain control, redirection, environmental changes, supervision, low bed, alarms, and activity (HLT-06, ADM-03).

Bed rails, lap trays, belts, vests, geriatric chairs with locked trays, mittens and any item the resident cannot remove are treated as possible restraints. The delegating nurse reviews each device, including bed rails requested by the resident or family, and records whether it is a restraint.

A restraint is used only with a written physician's order that states the purpose, type and duration. Staff do not accept a verbal order unless the program's procedure for verbal orders is followed and the written order is obtained promptly. The order is filed in the resident record.
Staff reject any PRN restraint order and ask the physician for a new order that meets this policy.
The delegating nurse obtains informed consent from the resident or representative as the law and program policy require, explains the risks, and updates the service plan (ADM-04).

The delegating nurse trains each staff member who may apply or monitor a restraint before the first use, and at least annually: how to apply it correctly, how to watch for skin, circulation and breathing problems, how to reposition and toilet the resident, and how to remove it in an emergency. Training is documented (STF-03).
The Manager or delegating nurse notifies the family or representative each time a restraint is used, and records the date, time and person reached.

A resident in a restraint is observed continuously or at the interval ordered. The resident is repositioned and offered toileting at least every 2 hours, and food, fluids, range of motion and comfort are offered. Each check is documented with time and staff initials.

The delegating nurse reviews the resident and the restraint at least weekly for skin condition, mobility, behavior, mood and continued need (HLT-07). The restraint is removed as soon as the cause is gone.

The restraint order is renewed by the physician every 7 calendar days. The delegating nurse tracks the expiration date. If the order is not renewed in time, the restraint is removed and the Manager is told.

Medications used to control behavior are given only on a practitioner's order for a diagnosed condition, with a documented target symptom and review. A psychotropic or sedating drug used only for discipline or convenience is a chemical restraint. Staff report any such order to the delegating nurse, who contacts the prescriber (HLT-01, HLT-02).

For a resident under hospice care, the delegating nurse coordinates any restraint order with the hospice and the practitioner before it is used. The hospice and the program each follow their own rules (COMAR 10.07.14.38H, COMAR 10.07.21; HLT-08).

Emergency use is limited to the shortest time needed to protect a resident from immediate harm. Staff call the practitioner and the delegating nurse at once for an order and call 911 if needed. The event is reported on an incident report within 24 hours (SAF-02).
The Manager reviews all restraints and bed-rail use monthly and presents results at QA (GOV-04). The goal is to reduce and eliminate restraint use.
Every restraint event, injury or suspected misuse is investigated. Substantiated misuse leads to discipline and, where required, reports under SAF-01.

responsibilities.duty: Prohibits restraint for discipline or convenience, ensures orders are valid and renewed, and reviews restraint use monthly.
Assesses need, tries alternatives, trains staff, monitors every restraint weekly, and coordinates with the practitioner and hospice.
Writes the order stating purpose, type and duration, and renews it every 7 calendar days when still needed.
Apply and monitor only as trained, reposition and toilet at least every 2 hours, document, and report concerns.
Take part in decisions and are notified each time a restraint is used.

documentation: Nursing assessment and record of alternatives tried
Physician's order with purpose, type, duration and 7-day renewals
Informed consent or discussion record
Notification record for each use
2-hour reposition and toileting log
Weekly nursing review
Staff training records
Monthly restraint and bed-rail review for QA

policies.title: Emergency and Disaster Plan
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff (including relief and contract staff), residents, resident representatives and visitors
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] can protect residents, keep services going and account for every person during a fire, severe weather, power or utility loss, public health emergency or other disaster. The plan gives staff clear instructions to evacuate, shelter in place, notify others and continue care for at least 72 hours.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(k) — Emergency and Disaster Plan, and the emergency preparedness requirements of COMAR 10.07.14.47. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written Emergency Preparedness Packet that is current, kept on site where all staff can reach it, and reviewed at least annually. The Packet covers: (1) evacuation; (2) shelter in place; (3) notification of residents' representatives, emergency services, OHCQ and others; (4) 72-hour continuity of care and operations; (5) a resident and visitor tracking system; and (6) a medical fact sheet for each resident. [AGENCY NAME] holds written agreements for evacuation sites and for transportation to those sites. Every staff member is oriented to the plan within 24 hours of beginning work. Disaster drills are held twice a year (semiannually) on all shifts, and drill records are kept for 2 years. If the program is licensed for 50 or more residents, a generator is installed and maintained. The Emergency Preparedness Packet is consistent with NFPA 101 and local codes (see SAF-06).

definitions.definition: The written, on-site set of plans and tools that covers evacuation, shelter in place, notification, 72-hour continuity, the tracking system and the resident medical fact sheets.
Keeping residents and staff safely inside the building, or in a protected area of it, when leaving would be more dangerous than staying.
The ability to keep providing food, water, medications, personal care, nursing oversight, heat or cooling, communication and safety for at least 72 hours without outside resupply or utilities.
The method staff use to know where every resident, staff member and visitor is during an emergency and to account for each person at an evacuation site.

A one-page summary for each resident (diagnoses, allergies, medications, diet, mobility and cognitive status, advance directive status, physician and representative contacts) that travels with the resident during evacuation.
A practice of the emergency plan for non-fire events (for example, severe weather, power outage, shelter in place or evacuation). Fire drills are covered in SAF-06.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) assembles and maintains the Emergency Preparedness Packet. It is stored at [LOCATION OF PACKET] and a copy is kept off site at [OFF-SITE LOCATION OR ELECTRONIC STORAGE].

The Packet includes sections for evacuation, shelter in place, notification, 72-hour continuity, the tracking system and the medical fact sheets. It also includes the emergency contact list (911, local emergency management, utilities, OHCQ at (410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005, pharmacy, delegating nurse, physicians and resident representatives).

The Manager completes a hazard review of the location and region (for example, fire, flood, winter storm, heat, power outage, hurricane or wind event, infectious disease outbreak and loss of water) and writes specific response steps for each hazard identified.

The Manager signs written agreements with at least one primary evacuation site and, where practical, an alternate site, and with a transportation provider able to move all residents, including those who use wheelchairs or need stretchers. Copies of the agreements are kept in the Packet and renewed when they expire or the parties change.

For each resident, the Delegating Nurse or Manager prepares a medical fact sheet at admission. It is updated at each service plan review and after any significant change in condition. A current set is kept in the Packet and in a grab-and-go binder at [LOCATION].

The 72-hour continuity section lists the supplies stored on site (drinking water, shelf-stable food that meets resident diets, a medication supply plan with the pharmacy, flashlights, batteries, incontinence and hygiene supplies, blankets and a battery or crank radio). It also lists how oxygen, refrigerated medications and other electrically powered equipment will be supported. The Manager checks supplies and expiration dates every [FREQUENCY, e.g., 6 months] and records the check.

If the program is licensed for 50 or more residents, the Manager makes sure a generator is installed, serviced and tested as the manufacturer and code require, and documents each test. If the program is licensed for fewer than 50 residents, the Packet documents how essential power needs will be met during an outage.

The tracking system uses a current resident roster, the staff schedule and a visitor sign-in log (see SAF-09). In an evacuation, the charge staff member assigns a staff member to take the roster, medical fact sheets and the medication supply, and checks each person off at the evacuation site by name.

The notification section directs staff to call 911 first when life or safety is at risk. The Manager or designee then notifies resident representatives, the Delegating Nurse, OHCQ and other required parties, and records the time and person reached.

Each new staff member, including relief and contract staff, is oriented to the Packet, the location of exits, shelter areas, extinguishers, the roster and the medical fact sheets within 24 hours of beginning work. The staff member signs and dates an orientation record, which is placed in the personnel file.

The Manager schedules disaster drills so that at least two are held each year (semiannually) and every shift (day, evening and night) takes part. Drills rotate through the hazard types in the Packet, including at least one drill involving evacuation or relocation steps and one involving shelter in place.

During each drill, the Manager or designee records the date, time, shift, type of scenario, staff and residents who took part, time to complete key steps, problems found and corrective actions. The Manager signs the drill record the same day.
Drill records are kept for 2 years and made available to OHCQ on request.

During an actual emergency, the highest-ranking staff member on site acts as incident lead until the Manager arrives. The incident lead activates the Packet, accounts for all residents, protects medications and records, and keeps a written log of actions and times.

After any actual emergency or drill, the Manager meets with staff within [NUMBER, e.g., 7] days to review what worked and what did not. Changes are made to the Packet and staff are told of the changes. The results are reported to the QA committee (GOV-04).

At least once a year, and after any significant change in the building, population served, evacuation site or transportation provider, the Manager reviews and updates the whole Packet. The Manager signs and dates the review and keeps prior versions under document control (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Provides resources for supplies, equipment, a generator where required, and agreements needed to carry out the plan.

Writes, maintains and annually reviews the Packet; holds the evacuation site and transportation agreements; schedules and records drills; orients staff; leads or delegates incident command; reports to OHCQ.
Carries out the Manager's duties under this policy when the Manager is absent.
Helps prepare and update resident medical fact sheets and the medication continuity plan; advises on clinical needs in evacuation or shelter in place.

responsibilities.role: Direct care staff and certified medication technicians
responsibilities.duty: Know the plan, take part in drills, keep the roster and fact sheets accessible, and follow the incident lead's directions.
Check emergency supplies, lighting, generator and utility shutoffs as assigned and report deficiencies to the Manager.

documentation: Current Emergency Preparedness Packet with annual review sign-off and version history
Signed evacuation site and transportation agreements
Resident medical fact sheets
Emergency supply check records and generator service and test records (if applicable)
Staff orientation records showing completion within 24 hours of starting work
Disaster drill records for all shifts, kept 2 years
Incident log and post-event review for any actual emergency
Visitor sign-in logs and roster used by the tracking system

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, residents, visitors and contractors
policies.purpose: To protect residents, staff and visitors from fire and scald hazards by keeping the building code-compliant, equipment serviced, staff trained and evacuation practiced on every shift.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] complies with NFPA 101 and applicable local fire and building codes, including Chapter 24 where the program is housed in a one- or two-family dwelling (COMAR 10.07.14.47). Fire extinguishers are placed on each floor and in special hazard areas (for example, the kitchen, laundry, furnace or mechanical room and any area where flammables or oxygen are stored) and are serviced at least annually by a licensee of the State Fire Marshal. All staff are trained in the use of fire extinguishers when hired and every year. Fire drills are held quarterly on all shifts, and records are kept for 2 years. Any fire or building code citation is reported to OHCQ within 7 days. Resident hot water is kept at 100–120°F at the fixture, with anti-scald or mixing valves, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.43.

definitions.definition: The Life Safety Code published by the National Fire Protection Association, adopted for assisted living through COMAR 10.07.14.47.
A location with greater fire risk, such as a kitchen, laundry, boiler or furnace room, or an area where oxygen, flammable liquids or other combustibles are used or stored.
A timed practice of fire alarm response, relocation or evacuation of residents, and staff roles, conducted as if a real fire were occurring.
A device that limits water temperature at the fixture to prevent burns.

procedures: Before opening and whenever the building or its use changes, the Manager confirms with the local fire authority and OHCQ that the building meets NFPA 101 and local codes, including Chapter 24 if it is a one- or two-family dwelling, and keeps copies of inspection reports and approvals.
The Manager posts evacuation floor plans showing exits, routes, extinguisher locations and assembly points on each floor, and each resident's room has the plan appropriate to that area.

Maintenance staff inspect exit routes, exit signs, emergency lighting, smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and the fire alarm system every [FREQUENCY, e.g., month] and record the results. Exits are never blocked, locked in a manner that prevents egress, or used for storage.

The Manager contracts with a licensee of the State Fire Marshal to service every extinguisher at least once a year. Each extinguisher carries a current service tag, and the invoice or report is kept on file.
Extinguishers are placed on every floor and in each special hazard area. Staff check them monthly for charge, access and tag and initial a log.

The Manager or a qualified trainer teaches each new staff member how to use a fire extinguisher during orientation (within the first [NUMBER, e.g., 30] days at the latest, and before working alone) and repeats the training for all staff every year. The training record is signed and placed in the personnel file.

The Manager schedules fire drills at least quarterly (once every 3 months) and varies the times so that day, evening and night shifts are each included in the quarterly cycle. Each shift takes part in drills at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., once per year or as required by the local fire authority].

During a drill, staff sound the alarm, call or simulate calling 911, move residents to safety using the assigned method, close doors, use the roster to account for every resident, staff member and visitor, and meet at the assembly point.

The person running the drill records the date, time of day, shift, the alarm and evacuation times, who took part, any residents who needed extra help, any problems and corrective action. The Manager reviews and signs the record within 3 business days.
Drill records are kept for 2 years and made available to OHCQ and the fire authority on request.

The Manager records how each resident will evacuate (independent, with cue, with one-person assist, with two-person assist or other) in the resident's service plan or evacuation list and updates it after any change in mobility or cognition.

Smoking, open flames, candles, space heaters and cooking appliances in resident rooms are controlled according to the Smoking Policy (SAF-08) and posted house rules. Oxygen is stored and used as set out in SAF-08.

Maintenance staff check hot water temperatures at a sample of resident fixtures at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., monthly], including the fixture farthest from the heater, and record the readings. Temperatures must be 100–120°F at the fixture. The anti-scald or mixing valves are tested and adjusted as needed.
If water is outside 100–120°F, the Manager removes the fixture from use or restricts access to it until it is corrected, and records the date and fix.

If a fire or building code citation is issued by any authority, the Manager notifies OHCQ within 7 days, records the date and the person notified, develops a plan of correction and keeps proof of correction. The report is also logged under REC-03.
After any actual fire, alarm activation or near miss, the Manager completes an incident report (SAF-02), reviews the response with staff and updates this policy or the emergency plan if needed.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures code compliance, extinguisher servicing, staff training, quarterly drills on all shifts, record retention and the 7-day report to OHCQ.
Covers these duties in the Manager's absence.
Inspect alarms, exits, lighting and extinguishers; test hot water and anti-scald valves; report and fix hazards.

responsibilities.role: Direct care staff and certified medication technicians
responsibilities.duty: Complete extinguisher training, take part in drills, follow evacuation steps and keep exits clear.
Funds corrections needed to meet code and to maintain safe water temperatures.

documentation: Fire authority inspection reports, building approvals and any citations with plans of correction
Extinguisher service tags and the annual service report from the State Fire Marshal licensee
Monthly extinguisher and exit/alarm check logs
Staff extinguisher training records (initial and annual)
Quarterly fire drill records for all shifts, kept 2 years
Hot water temperature logs and valve maintenance records
Evacuation plans and individual resident evacuation needs
Copy of the 7-day report to OHCQ for any fire or building code citation

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, residents, visitors, volunteers and contractors
policies.purpose: To prevent the spread of infection among residents, staff and visitors through screening, immunity, vaccination, hygiene, cleaning, training and a bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an infection prevention and control program that is reviewed through the Quality Assurance Plan (COMAR 10.07.14.13). The program includes an annual tuberculosis (TB) risk assessment, TB screening and evidence of MMR and varicella immunity for the Manager and all staff (COMAR 10.07.14.15 and 10.07.14.19), and documented flu and COVID-19 vaccination status, with vaccines advised for staff (COMAR 10.07.14.20). Staff receive training in infection control and food safety initially and every year. [AGENCY NAME] follows a written Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan under 29 CFR 1910.1030. Visitor and activity restrictions during an outbreak are documented.

definitions.definition: A yearly written review of the program's TB risk (for example, community rates, resident and staff history, and past exposures) that decides what screening is needed. It is done as part of the QA program.

Basic infection control practices used with all residents, including hand hygiene, gloves and other personal protective equipment (PPE), safe handling of sharps and linens, and cleaning of surfaces and equipment.
A contact with blood or other potentially infectious material through the eyes, mouth, mucous membrane, non-intact skin or a sharps injury.

Two or more residents or staff with the same illness (for example, influenza, COVID-19, norovirus, scabies) within a short period, or any cluster the local health department says to treat as an outbreak.

procedures: Before a new hire or the Manager starts work, the Manager obtains evidence of TB screening and proof of MMR and varicella immunity (or a documented physician-reviewed alternative) and places it in the personnel file (see STF-04 and STF-05). Staff who lack immunity are handled as directed by the physician or the local health department.

The Manager offers or advises each employee to receive a yearly flu vaccine and the COVID-19 vaccine and records the employee's status (vaccinated, declined, or medical or other exemption) in the personnel file. Declinations are signed.

At least once a year, the Manager completes a written TB risk assessment, using a template approved by the QA committee, and records any change in screening needs. The assessment is reviewed at the annual QA meeting (GOV-04).

Residents are screened for signs and symptoms of TB and other communicable diseases at admission according to ADM-01 and the physician's or nurse practitioner's orders, and results are placed in the resident's record.

All staff receive infection control and food safety training at orientation and at least annually. The training covers standard precautions, hand hygiene, PPE, cleaning and disinfection, laundry and waste handling, food handling and reporting of illness. Attendance is recorded and filed under STF-03.

Staff perform hand hygiene before and after resident contact, before handling food or medications, after using the toilet and after removing gloves. Alcohol-based hand rub, soap, paper towels and gloves are stocked at every point of care.

Staff do not work while they have symptoms of a contagious illness (for example, fever, vomiting, diarrhea or a new cough with fever) and must report symptoms to the Manager or Alternate Manager before the shift. The Manager decides on return to work in line with physician and health department advice, and logs the absence.

The Delegating Nurse reviews residents' signs of infection at each visit. Staff report new infection symptoms (fever, cough, diarrhea, rash, urinary symptoms, wound drainage) to the nurse and the physician as set out in HLT-04, and begin isolation or droplet or contact precautions as instructed.
The Manager keeps a log of resident and staff infections (date, type, unit or room, actions taken and notifications) and reviews it monthly for patterns.

Housekeeping and laundry follow DL-03. Surfaces such as handrails, door handles and bathrooms are cleaned daily with an EPA-registered disinfectant used per label directions. Soiled linens are bagged at the point of use and washed separately from clean items.

Under the Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan, the Manager identifies staff tasks with possible exposure (for example, fingerstick glucose testing, wound care, handling soiled items), provides PPE, sharps containers and hepatitis B vaccination offers, and trains staff at hire and annually.

After an exposure incident, the staff member washes the area immediately, reports to the Manager, and is sent for medical evaluation and follow-up the same day. The Manager completes an incident report (SAF-02) and records the follow-up in a confidential medical file separate from the personnel file.

In an outbreak, the Manager contacts the local health department and the resident's physicians, starts any isolation or cohorting recommended, increases cleaning, may limit group activities or visitors as the health department advises, and notifies residents and representatives. Required reports are made under REC-03.

Any restriction on visitors or activities during an outbreak is documented with the date, reason, the people restricted, the authority advising it and the date it ended, and is applied in a way that respects residents' rights (see SAF-09 and RR-01).
The Manager reviews infection prevention results, the infection log and any pharmacist or other findings at the QA meeting (GOV-04), and updates this policy and training as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees the infection control program; completes the annual TB risk assessment; ensures staff screening, immunity and vaccination records; arranges training; manages outbreak response and reports.
Assesses residents for infection signs, advises staff on precautions, communicates with physicians and helps with training and the exposure control plan.

responsibilities.role: Direct care staff and certified medication technicians
responsibilities.duty: Follow standard precautions, report symptoms in themselves or residents, use PPE correctly and complete training.

responsibilities.role: Housekeeping, laundry and food service staff
responsibilities.duty: Clean, disinfect and handle laundry and food safely as trained.
Reviews the annual TB risk assessment, infection log and trends.

documentation: Annual TB risk assessment and QA minutes
Staff TB screening, MMR/varicella evidence and flu/COVID-19 vaccine status or declination forms in personnel files
Infection control and food safety training records
Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan, hepatitis B vaccination offer records and training records
Exposure incident reports and confidential follow-up records
Infection log and outbreak records including health department contacts
Documentation of any visitor or activity restrictions during an outbreak

policies.title: Smoking Policy
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] residents, staff, visitors and contractors
policies.purpose: To set out clearly whether smoking is permitted at [AGENCY NAME] and, where permitted, the fire-safe rules, designated areas and resident assessments that protect everyone from fire and smoke.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(j) — Smoking Policy, and COMAR 10.07.14.48. [AGENCY NAME]'s smoking status is: [SELECT ONE — OPTION A: Smoking is NOT permitted inside the building or on the grounds, by residents, staff or visitors. / OPTION B: Smoking is permitted only in the designated area(s) described in this policy]. This status is stated in the Uniform Disclosure Statement and Resident Agreement (RR-04) and explained to each applicant before admission. If smoking is permitted, [AGENCY NAME] sets fire-safe rules and designated smoking areas, prohibits smoking anywhere oxygen or flammables are used or stored, and completes a smoking assessment for each resident who smokes. The assessment is recorded in the service plan and reassessed at least annually. Fire safety follows COMAR 10.07.14.47 (see SAF-06).

definitions.definition: A specific location, identified in writing and by signage, where smoking is allowed under this policy (applies only if smoking is permitted).

A written evaluation of a resident's ability to smoke safely, including cognition, judgment, vision, dexterity, ability to handle lighters or cigarettes, history of burns or unsafe smoking and need for supervision.
Cigarettes, cigars, pipes, lighters, matches and similar items (including electronic cigarettes and vaping devices, which are treated the same way under this policy).
Any place where oxygen is stored or used, or where flammable or combustible liquids, gases or materials are used or stored.

procedures: The Governing Body and Manager decide whether smoking is permitted and enter the decision above and in the Uniform Disclosure Statement. Any change is approved in writing, residents and representatives are given advance notice, and the Disclosure Statement is updated (RR-04, GOV-03).

During pre-admission screening (ADM-01), the Manager or designee asks every applicant whether they smoke or vape and explains [AGENCY NAME]'s smoking status. An applicant who smokes is not admitted if the program does not permit smoking and the applicant is unwilling to comply, and the reason is documented.

Signs stating the smoking rule are posted at each entrance and, if permitted, in the designated area. 'No Smoking – Oxygen in Use' signs are posted on the door of any room where oxygen is in use and in any oxygen storage area.

OPTION A (no smoking): Staff remind residents and visitors of the rule. Residents who wish to smoke are supported in discussing options with their physician and may be offered cessation resources. Smoking materials found in the building are held for safekeeping or removed, as agreed in the resident agreement.

OPTION B (designated areas): The Manager designates each smoking area at least [DISTANCE, e.g., 25 feet] from building entrances, windows, air intakes, oxygen storage and combustible materials. Each area has non-combustible ashtrays or receptacles with a lid, a fire extinguisher or hose within reach, adequate lighting and seating, and shelter from weather.
OPTION B: Smoking is allowed only during hours posted as [SMOKING HOURS]. Staff do not smoke with residents while on duty and smoke only on breaks in a designated staff area away from residents.

OPTION B: Matches, lighters and loose smoking materials of residents who cannot manage them safely are stored by staff in a locked container and given out for use under supervision, as set in the service plan.

OPTION B: Smoking is never allowed in resident rooms, bathrooms, hallways, kitchens or common areas, in a bed or recliner, while using or near oxygen, or in any place where flammables are used or stored. Residents who use oxygen do not smoke while it is on or within [DISTANCE, e.g., 10 feet] of the oxygen source.

OPTION B: Before a resident who smokes is admitted, and again whenever there is a significant change in condition (for example, new confusion, sedating medication, a fall, vision loss or oxygen use), the Delegating Nurse or Manager completes the smoking assessment and records the result in the resident's record.

OPTION B: The assessment result and any needed safeguards (supervision, smoking apron, no unsupervised access to lighters, staff light and extinguish, use of a designated area only) are written into the service plan (ADM-04). The assessment is repeated and the service plan updated at least once a year.

OPTION B: A resident who is assessed as unsafe to smoke independently is told the reason, the options and the supervision available, and the resident or representative is included in the service plan meeting. The Manager offers alternatives (nicotine replacement options discussed with the physician, or discussion of whether the program can meet the resident's needs under ADM-05).

If a resident, visitor or staff member is found smoking in a prohibited area, staff immediately extinguish the material, make sure no fire has started, tell the person of the rule, and notify the Manager. The Manager completes an incident report (SAF-02) and takes action through the resident agreement or the staff conduct policy (STF-06).
Staff are trained on this policy at orientation and annually, including how to recognise unsafe smoking and what to do in a fire (SAF-06).
The Manager reviews smoking-related incidents, near misses and the smoking area inspection log at least annually as part of QA (GOV-04) and revises this policy as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether smoking is permitted and approves any change.
Applies and enforces the policy; designates and inspects smoking areas; ensures assessments, service plan entries and annual reassessments are done; informs applicants.
Completes or oversees smoking assessments and recommends safeguards.

responsibilities.role: Direct care staff and certified medication technicians
responsibilities.duty: Follow safeguards in the service plan, supervise as directed, secure smoking materials and report violations.
Follow posted rules and safeguards in the service plan.

documentation: Smoking status entry in the Uniform Disclosure Statement and Resident Agreement
Smoking assessments and annual reassessments, and the resulting service plan entries
Posted signage and designated area inspection log (if smoking is permitted)
Staff training records on this policy
Incident reports for smoking violations or burns
QA review of smoking-related incidents

policies.title: Visitors and Pets
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] residents, representatives, visitors, volunteers, staff and any animals on the premises
policies.purpose: To protect each resident's right to see family, friends and others while keeping everyone safe and accounted for, and to allow animals in a way that is safe, healthy and respectful of residents' needs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] respects residents' access to visitors as provided in the Resident Bill of Rights (COMAR 10.07.14.36). Visiting hours are [VISITING HOURS, e.g., open to residents' preference], and visits at other times are allowed by arrangement so long as the safety and rights of other residents are protected. All visitors sign in and out so that the tracking system can account for everyone in an emergency (COMAR 10.07.14.47; see SAF-05). Pets are permitted only under the conditions in this policy: allergy consideration, current vaccination records, and exclusion from food preparation areas. Any restriction on visitors or pets during an outbreak or other health event is documented and limited to what is necessary.

definitions.definition: Any person who is not a resident or a scheduled staff member, including family, friends, volunteers, clergy, health care providers, contractors and ombudsman or agency representatives.
An animal owned by a resident and approved to live at the program with that resident.
An animal owned by a visitor, staff member or the program that is brought for visits or lives in a common area.

A dog (or other animal as the law allows) individually trained to do work or perform tasks for a person with a disability. Service animals are not pets and are handled under the program's nondiscrimination policy (RR-08).

procedures: At admission, the Manager or designee gives residents and representatives the visiting rules and this policy, and explains them. Residents may say who they do and do not want to see, and staff respect and record those preferences in the service plan or resident record.
A sign-in log is kept at the main entrance. Each visitor writes their name, the resident visited, the time in and the time out. Staff remind visitors to sign out when they leave.

Staff do not deny entry to a visitor the resident wants to see unless there is a safety, infection control or legal reason. The Manager is told of any proposed restriction, and the reason, date and resident's views are documented (see RR-01).

Authorized representatives of OHCQ, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and other agencies with legal access are admitted as set out in RR-03 and are not delayed. They are asked to sign in and out for emergency tracking only.
Visitors who show signs of illness (fever, cough, vomiting, diarrhea) are asked to reschedule. Staff offer masks, hand rub and instructions when appropriate (SAF-07).
Visitors are asked not to bring food that conflicts with a resident's therapeutic diet (DL-01) or to give medications to residents. Staff tell the nurse of any concern.

Staff may ask a visitor to leave, and the Manager may restrict a visitor, only when the visitor's behavior threatens the safety or rights of residents or staff. The Manager records the incident and decision, informs the resident, and notifies the police if there is a threat or suspected abuse (SAF-01).
During an emergency, staff use the sign-in log with the roster to account for each visitor at the assembly point (SAF-05, SAF-06).

During an outbreak or other health emergency, the Manager may limit visiting only as advised by the health department or physician. The restriction is documented with the date, reason, authority and end date, residents and representatives are informed, and alternatives such as outdoor visits, window visits, phone and video calls are offered.

Resident pet request: The resident or representative submits a written request to the Manager before bringing a pet. The Manager reviews it with the Delegating Nurse and considers the resident's ability to care for the pet, other residents' allergies, fears or health conditions, and the building's layout.

A pet must have proof of current vaccinations (including rabies where required by law) and a recent veterinary check, kept on file. The Manager asks about aggression and any bite history, and may decline an animal that poses a danger.

Pets are not allowed in kitchens, food storage, food preparation or dining areas while food is prepared or served, or in medication rooms or laundry. Service animals follow applicable law, and their access is handled under RR-08.

The resident (or representative) is responsible for feeding, walking, waste cleanup and veterinary care of a resident pet, and for any damage. Staff are not required to care for a pet except as listed in the service plan. Staff wash hands after contact with animals.
Visiting pets must be leashed or in a carrier, accompanied by the owner, and restricted to areas approved by the Manager. Residents with allergies or fear of animals are not required to be near them.
The Manager removes an animal when it shows aggression, is a health or safety risk, causes a documented allergic reaction, or the owner fails to follow the rules, and informs the owner in writing.
The Manager reviews visitor and pet concerns annually and reports patterns to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Applies this policy, approves pets, decides on any visitor restrictions and documents them.

responsibilities.role: Direct care staff and certified medication technicians
responsibilities.duty: Welcome visitors, ensure sign-in, protect residents' privacy and report concerns or safety problems.
Advises on infection control restrictions and on health and allergy aspects of pets.
Tell staff whom they do and do not want to see, and care for any resident pet.
Sign in and out, follow posted rules and infection control instructions.

documentation: Visitor sign-in logs
Residents' stated visitor preferences in the record or service plan
Documentation of any visitor restriction, with reason, authority and dates
Written pet requests, approvals, vaccination records and any removal notice
Outbreak-related restriction records
QA review notes on visitor and pet issues

policies.title: Food Service, Menus, Therapeutic Diets and 4-Week Menu Cycle
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] food service staff, direct care staff, the Delegating Nurse, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident receives safe, nutritious, appealing meals and snacks that meet their needs and preferences, and that menus and diets are planned, reviewed by a qualified professional and documented.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 6 — 4-week menu cycle for a regular diet with written documentation from a licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist that the menu is nutritionally adequate. [AGENCY NAME] serves three meals plus snacks every day (COMAR 10.07.14.30). Menus are written a week ahead, posted where residents can see them, and kept for 6 months. A licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist reviews the 4-week regular-diet menu cycle before licensure and at least every 3 years, and the written documentation is kept on file. Therapeutic diets are served only on the order of an authorized practitioner and are carried into the service plan (COMAR 10.07.14.28). Programs with a licensed capacity of 17 or more beds also meet the requirements of COMAR 10.15.03, Food service facilities. [AGENCY NAME]'s licensed capacity is [LICENSED CAPACITY]; the Manager records here whether COMAR 10.15.03 applies: [APPLIES / DOES NOT APPLY]. Programs with fewer than 17 beds follow the basic food safety requirements of COMAR 10.07.14 and any directive from OHCQ or the local health jurisdiction.

definitions.definition: A set of four weeks of daily menus for a regular diet (breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks) that repeats, with seasonal changes as needed.

A diet ordered by an authorized practitioner for a medical condition, such as diabetic/consistent carbohydrate, low sodium, renal, pureed, mechanical soft, thickened liquids or gluten-free for celiac disease.
A professional licensed in Maryland to practice dietetics or nutrition who reviews and signs off on the menus.
A food or beverage offered between meals and at bedtime according to resident need and preference.
A written or documented order from a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant or other authorized prescriber.

procedures: Before licensure, the Manager prepares a 4-week regular-diet menu cycle for breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks that reflects the foods and ethnic, cultural and religious preferences of the residents the program serves.

The Manager sends the 4-week menu cycle to a licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist, who reviews it and provides a signed, dated written statement that the menu is nutritionally adequate. The statement includes the reviewer's name, license number and the date, and is attached to the OHCQ application (Step Three, item 6).

The Manager keeps the dietitian or nutritionist's written documentation on file and has the menu reviewed again at least every 3 years, and sooner if the menu cycle changes substantially or the resident population changes. The next review date is entered on the compliance calendar: [DATE].
The Manager or cook writes each week's menu one week in advance, based on the approved cycle. Substitutions are made only with foods of similar nutritional value and are recorded on the posted menu.

Menus are posted weekly in the dining area or another place easily seen by residents and representatives. Copies of the menus, including substitutions, are kept for 6 months and made available to OHCQ on request.

[AGENCY NAME] serves three meals each day plus snacks. Fresh water and appropriate beverages are available at all times, and snacks (including at bedtime) are offered daily and for residents who miss a meal. The meal and snack times are posted: [MEAL TIMES].

At pre-admission screening and admission, the Manager or Delegating Nurse records each resident's food preferences, allergies, intolerances, cultural or religious practices, chewing and swallowing ability and any weight concerns. This is carried into the Resident Assessment Tool and service plan (ADM-03, ADM-04).

A therapeutic or modified diet is begun only after a practitioner order is received and placed in the resident's record. The order is reviewed whenever the resident's condition changes and at least at each service plan review.

The Delegating Nurse and Manager include special care needs that involve diet (for example, diabetes, swallowing problems, enteral feeding, weight loss) in the service plan and tell the cook and direct care staff in writing. Diet cards or lists are updated and kept in the kitchen and used at service.

For therapeutic diets, the cook uses recipes and portions that match the order, with menus adapted from the regular cycle. The Manager obtains advice from a dietitian or nutritionist when a diet cannot reasonably be adapted from the regular menu.

Staff serve meals at safe temperatures, assist residents who need help eating or have swallowing precautions, and watch for coughing, choking or reduced intake. They record meals refused or poorly eaten, and report weight loss or dehydration to the Delegating Nurse (HLT-04).

Residents are weighed on admission and at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., monthly] or as ordered. A weight change of [PERCENT, e.g., 5% in 30 days or 10% in 6 months] is reported to the nurse and physician and addressed in the service plan.

Food is purchased from approved sources, stored at safe temperatures (cold at or below 41°F, frozen at 0°F, hot holding at 135°F or above), labeled and dated, and protected from contamination. Refrigerator and freezer temperatures are logged daily. Staff follow safe handwashing and illness-reporting rules (SAF-07).

Food service staff complete food safety training at hire and annually, and the records are filed under STF-03. Where COMAR 10.15.03 applies, the kitchen is operated and inspected as that chapter requires, and any licenses, permits and inspection reports are posted or kept on file. Where it does not apply, the Manager follows any directive from OHCQ or the local health jurisdiction.

Residents or representatives may make food suggestions or complaints to any staff member or through the Resident Council or grievance procedure (RR-02). The Manager reviews comments at least monthly, adjusts menus within the approved cycle and reports patterns to the QA committee (GOV-04).
The Manager records the menu review dates, the posted weekly menus, diet orders and temperature logs, and checks them quarterly to confirm they are complete and current.
