responsibilities.duty: Ensures the 4-week menu cycle is written and reviewed by a licensed dietitian or nutritionist before licensure and every 3 years; ensures weekly menus are written, posted and retained 6 months; ensures food safety and applicable COMAR 10.15.03 compliance.

responsibilities.role: Licensed Dietitian or Nutritionist ([NAME AND LICENSE NUMBER])
responsibilities.duty: Reviews and signs the 4-week menu cycle for nutritional adequacy and advises on therapeutic diets.
Ensures diet orders are obtained, reflected in the service plan and communicated to the kitchen, and monitors weights, swallowing and intake.
Prepare and serve meals according to the menu and diet orders, follow safe food handling, keep logs and post menus.

responsibilities.role: Direct care staff and certified medication technicians
responsibilities.duty: Assist residents at meals, follow diet and swallowing precautions, and report intake or weight concerns.
Share preferences, allergies and concerns and take part in service plan meetings.

documentation: Signed 4-week menu cycle and the written documentation from the licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist (name, license number, date); later 3-year reviews
Weekly written and posted menus with substitutions, retained 6 months
Practitioner diet orders and diet lists
Resident food preferences, allergies and weight records
Service plan entries for diet-related needs
Refrigerator, freezer and hot-holding temperature logs
Food safety training records and any food service inspection reports (where COMAR 10.15.03 applies)
Resident or representative food comments and responses

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
policies.applies_to: All residents; Activity Coordinator, direct care staff, Assisted Living Manager and delegating nurse
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident is offered meaningful social, recreational, spiritual and physical activities that match the resident's assessed interests, abilities and choices, and that participation is always voluntary.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] offers a planned program of activities every week. The activities are based on the interests and needs identified in each resident's Resident Assessment Tool and service plan (COMAR 10.07.14.28). Participation is voluntary. A resident may decline any activity, and declining does not affect the resident's care, standing or services. A resident is never required to perform work for the program. A resident may work only with the resident's consent and with compensation, as protected by the Resident Bill of Rights (COMAR 10.07.14.36). Residents and their representatives are invited to take part in service plan meetings where activity preferences are reviewed. A monthly activity calendar and participation notes are kept. Activities are adapted for residents with cognitive impairment, sensory loss or mobility limits.

definitions.definition: Any planned or spontaneous social, recreational, creative, physical, spiritual, educational or community event offered by the program.
A brief dated entry recording who took part in an activity, the level of engagement and any refusal or change in mood or behavior.
Any task a resident performs that benefits the program or other residents. It may occur only with the resident's consent and compensation.

procedures: At admission and at each reassessment, the Assisted Living Manager or delegating nurse asks the resident and representative about past and current interests, routines, faith practices, hobbies, preferred times of day and preferred group size, and records the answers in the Resident Assessment Tool and service plan.

Within 30 calendar days of admission, the service plan states the activity interests and any supports the resident needs, such as seating, hearing or vision aids, cueing or one-to-one help (COMAR 10.07.14.28).

The Activity Coordinator builds a monthly activity calendar before the first day of each month. It offers a mix of social, physical, cognitive, creative, spiritual and community activities, and includes activities at different times of day, including weekends.

The Activity Coordinator includes at least some activities for residents who prefer to stay in their rooms or who have limited mobility or cognitive impairment, such as one-to-one visits, music, reading or sensory activities.
The Activity Coordinator posts the calendar in a common area and gives each resident a copy on request. Large-print copies are provided for residents who need them.
Staff invite each resident personally and remind residents of events. Staff help residents get to and from activities.

If a resident declines, staff respect the decision, offer an alternative and record the refusal. Repeated refusals or withdrawal are reported to the delegating nurse as a possible change in condition (see HLT-04).
Staff record participation notes for each activity at the end of the activity or by the end of the shift. Notes include date, activity, residents who took part, level of engagement and any concern.

The Activity Coordinator reviews participation notes monthly. Residents with little or no participation are flagged to the Assisted Living Manager and the resident's service plan interests are revisited with the resident.

The Assisted Living Manager and delegating nurse review activity preferences and participation at each six-month service plan review and at the annual and significant-change reassessments (COMAR 10.07.14.28).

The program never requires, pressures or schedules a resident to perform work for the program. If a resident asks to help with a task, the Assisted Living Manager documents the resident's voluntary consent, the task, and the agreed compensation before the work begins, and the resident may stop at any time (COMAR 10.07.14.36).
Residents may propose new activities, outings or groups at resident meetings or to any staff member. The Activity Coordinator responds within 14 days and records the outcome.
Outings are planned so that residents who need assistance are accompanied. Transportation is arranged under DL-04 and absences are tracked.
The Assisted Living Manager reviews the calendar and participation records at least quarterly as part of the quality assurance plan (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures an activity program is funded, staffed and delivered; approves the calendar; reviews participation records; protects the voluntary nature of participation and work.
Gathers interests, builds the monthly calendar, leads or arranges activities, and keeps participation notes.
Invite and assist residents, respect refusals, and record participation and concerns.
Reviews activity needs with the service plan and responds to reported changes in mood or participation.

documentation: Monthly activity calendars
Participation notes
Activity interests recorded in the Resident Assessment Tool and service plan
Resident work consent and compensation record, if any
Resident meeting notes and activity requests

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: All residents and the physical plant; housekeeping, laundry and maintenance staff and the Assisted Living Manager
policies.purpose: To keep the building, resident rooms, bathrooms, common areas, equipment and linens clean, safe and in good repair, and to meet the Maryland physical plant requirements for water temperature, space, bathrooms and assist rails.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a clean, safe, sanitary and homelike environment. Hot water available to residents is kept between 100°F and 120°F at the fixture, and anti-scald or mixing valves are installed and maintained (COMAR 10.07.14.43). Common space is provided at 35 square feet per licensed bed, and resident rooms and bathrooms meet the limits of COMAR 10.07.14.49–.51: no more than 2 residents per room, at least 80 square feet for a single room and 120 square feet for a double room, at least 1 toilet and sink for every 4 residents and 1 tub or shower for every 8 residents, with privacy latches on bathroom doors. Programs with 17 or more beds have assist rails on both sides of resident corridors (COMAR 10.07.14.46). Housekeeping, laundry and maintenance also follow the general physical plant and laundry requirements of COMAR 10.07.14. Repairs that affect resident health or safety are handled promptly. Residents' personal belongings are handled with respect and laundry is returned to the correct resident.

definitions.definition: Any faucet, shower head or tub spout from which a resident may draw hot water.
A device that limits or blends water temperature to prevent scalding.
A fixed rail along a corridor wall that residents may hold for stability while walking.
Living, dining, activity and similar areas available to all residents.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager prepares a written housekeeping and laundry schedule that lists daily, weekly and monthly tasks for resident rooms, bathrooms, common areas, kitchen areas and laundry, and assigns each task to a role.

Housekeeping staff clean resident rooms and bathrooms at least [FREQUENCY] and as needed after spills or soiling, using products and methods that follow SAF-07. Staff keep cleaning chemicals locked or otherwise out of residents' reach where a resident's cognitive status makes this necessary.
Staff respect residents' privacy: they knock and announce themselves before entering rooms, and residents may take part in keeping their own rooms tidy if they wish.

Laundry staff wash personal clothing and linens at least weekly and sooner as needed. Staff handle soiled linen with gloves and bag it at the point of use, and keep clean and soiled linen separated at all times (SAF-07).
Staff label or otherwise identify each resident's clothing so it is returned to the right resident. Staff report any lost or damaged item to the Assisted Living Manager the same day (RR-05).

The maintenance person checks hot water at a sample of resident fixtures at least monthly with a calibrated thermometer, and records the date, location and temperature. Any reading outside 100–120°F is reported to the Assisted Living Manager immediately and corrected before the fixture is used again by residents (COMAR 10.07.14.43).
The maintenance person inspects anti-scald or mixing valves at least quarterly and after any plumbing work, and records the result.

The Assisted Living Manager verifies at licensure and whenever a room or bathroom is changed that the building meets the standards in COMAR 10.07.14.49–.51: common space of 35 square feet per bed, no more than 2 residents per room, at least 80 or 120 square feet per room, and bathroom fixture ratios of 1 toilet and sink per 4 residents and 1 tub or shower per 8.
Bathroom doors have working privacy latches. Maintenance staff check them monthly and repair or replace any that fail within [NUMBER] days.

If the program has 17 or more beds, the maintenance person checks assist rails on both sides of resident corridors monthly for secure attachment and clear access, and records the check (COMAR 10.07.14.46).

Staff report maintenance needs on a written or electronic maintenance request log. The Assisted Living Manager reviews the log daily on business days and classifies each item as urgent, meaning a hazard to health or safety, or routine.
Urgent items are fixed or made safe immediately, for example by blocking off an area or moving a resident, and the repair is recorded. Routine items are completed within [NUMBER] days.
Maintenance and housekeeping staff keep walkways, exits and corridors clear, and report burned-out lights, damaged flooring, loose handrails and similar hazards at once.
The Assisted Living Manager conducts a documented walk-through of the whole building at least monthly and takes the results to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).
Pest control, trash removal and waste handling are carried out by schedule and recorded. Staff clean and disinfect shared equipment between residents as set out in SAF-07.
Records of water temperature checks, valve inspections, repairs and the housekeeping schedule are kept and available to OHCQ surveyors on request.

responsibilities.duty: Assigns staff and resources, reviews maintenance requests daily, confirms space and bathroom standards, and reviews monthly walk-through results.
Tests hot water, checks anti-scald valves, assist rails and privacy latches, performs repairs and keeps maintenance logs.
Perform scheduled cleaning and laundry, follow infection control practices, protect resident privacy and property, and report hazards.
Report spills, hazards, damaged equipment and water that is too hot or too cold immediately.

documentation: Housekeeping and laundry schedules
Monthly hot water temperature log
Anti-scald/mixing valve inspection record
Assist rail and privacy latch checks
Maintenance request and repair log
Monthly building walk-through reports
Floor plan showing room and common space measurements

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: All residents; staff drivers, the Assisted Living Manager and any contracted transportation provider
policies.purpose: To arrange safe, accessible and insured transportation for residents to appointments, activities and community outings and for emergency evacuation, and to account for every resident who leaves or returns to the building.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] helps residents arrange transportation as set out in the resident agreement and service plan. When the program transports residents in a vehicle it owns, leases or operates, it carries the insurance required of Medicaid assisted living waiver providers that transport residents (COMAR 10.09.54.05). Staff who drive residents hold a valid driver's license and are included in the criminal history records check and other screening (STF-02). The program keeps transportation agreements for evacuation so that residents can be moved in an emergency (COMAR 10.07.14.47). Transportation is provided without discrimination, and residents with disabilities receive reasonable accommodations consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101 et seq.). Every resident leaving or returning is recorded in the resident tracking system so that the program always knows who is in the building.

definitions.definition: An employee authorized by the Assisted Living Manager to drive a program vehicle or a personal vehicle for program-approved resident transportation.
The sign-out and sign-in log or electronic record used to account for each resident's whereabouts, also used during emergencies (SAF-05).
A written agreement with a transportation provider to move residents to an evacuation site in an emergency.

procedures: During pre-admission screening and at each reassessment, the Assisted Living Manager or delegating nurse records each resident's transportation needs, mobility aids, ability to ride independently and any need for an escort (ADM-01, ADM-03).

The Assisted Living Manager keeps current proof of the insurance that covers resident transportation, and confirms before any resident is driven that the vehicle and the driver are covered. The insurance policy is reviewed at each renewal.

Before a staff member is authorized to drive residents, the Assisted Living Manager copies the valid driver's license, confirms the criminal history records check and OIG exclusion check are complete under STF-02, and records authorization in the personnel file.

The Assisted Living Manager checks each authorized driver's license status at least annually and immediately if the driver reports a suspension or license issue. A driver whose license is not valid is removed from driving duties the same day.
Residents or representatives request transportation at least [NUMBER] days before the trip whenever possible. Staff record the date, time, destination, escort needs and equipment needed.

Staff confirm that the vehicle used is suitable for the resident. Residents who use wheelchairs or other mobility devices are transported in a vehicle with the appropriate lift or ramp and securement, and staff will not refuse transportation because of a disability when a reasonable accommodation is available.

Before each trip, the driver checks the vehicle for safety, fuel, seat belts and securement equipment, and a staff member confirms that the resident's medications, medical information and emergency contact information go with the resident if needed.

Each resident who leaves the building is signed out in the tracking system with the time, destination, escort and expected return. Each return is signed in. The staff member in charge reconciles the log at every shift change.
If a resident does not return by the expected time, staff call the resident, the escort or the destination within 30 minutes and follow SAF-03 if the resident cannot be located.

Staff keep residents' coordination with outside providers: for medical appointments, staff share the current medication list and any concerns with the provider and record any new orders on return (HLT-04, HLT-01).

The Assisted Living Manager keeps a signed transportation agreement with a provider that can move residents to the evacuation site named in the Emergency Preparedness Packet, reviews it at least annually with the emergency plan, and keeps a copy on site (COMAR 10.07.14.47; SAF-05).
Staff drivers must not use a hand-held phone while driving, must not drive while impaired, and must not transport more residents than the vehicle has seat belts for.
Any accident, injury or incident during transport is reported to the Assisted Living Manager immediately, emergency services are called if needed, and an incident report is completed under SAF-02.
Fees, if any, for transportation are stated in the resident agreement and fee schedule (RR-04). Medicaid waiver residents are not charged for services the waiver covers.
The Assisted Living Manager reviews transportation incidents, tracking logs and insurance annually as part of the quality assurance plan (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains insurance, authorizes and monitors drivers, keeps evacuation transportation agreements, and reviews tracking logs and incidents.
Hold a valid license, drive safely, secure residents and equipment, and sign residents out and in.
Identifies residents' transportation, escort and equipment needs and reviews information that goes to outside providers.
Reconcile the tracking system each shift and start the missing-resident procedure when a resident is overdue.

documentation: Proof of vehicle and transportation insurance
Driver authorization, license copy and annual license check
Transportation request log
Resident sign-out and sign-in tracking log
Evacuation transportation agreements
Incident reports involving transportation

policies.title: Adult Medical Day Care Policy
policies.applies_to: Residents who choose to attend adult medical day care; Assisted Living Manager, delegating nurse and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To state how [AGENCY NAME] treats a resident's attendance at an adult medical day care program, to make sure attendance is voluntary and disclosed in the resident agreement, and to coordinate medications, schedules and transportation between the program and the day care.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(h), p. 10 — Adult Medical Day Care Policy. Attendance at an adult medical day care program is voluntary. [AGENCY NAME] does not require, pressure or condition admission or continued residence on attendance (COMAR 10.07.14.36). The program's adult medical day care policy is disclosed in the resident agreement (RR-04). [AGENCY NAME] does not itself operate an adult medical day care program at this location unless it is separately authorized. For residents who choose to attend an outside day care, [AGENCY NAME] coordinates schedules, medications, transportation and communication so the resident's care is continuous. For Medicaid Community Options Waiver residents, the program understands that the assisted living waiver rates for W0226/W0227 assume no medical day care, and covered assisted living services under COMAR 10.09.54.13 are not duplicated by day care services. The Assisted Living Manager works with the resident's case manager before a waiver resident begins or stops day care attendance (GOV-06).

definitions.definition: A community-based program, separate from the assisted living program, that provides health, social and supportive services to adults during the day.
A written form that travels with the resident and lists schedule, medications, changes in condition and contacts for both programs.

procedures: At pre-admission and in the resident agreement, the Assisted Living Manager tells the resident and representative in plain language that attending adult medical day care is the resident's choice, that it is not a condition of admission or stay, and what the program's day care policy is (RR-04, COMAR 10.07.14.36).
The Assisted Living Manager records in the resident agreement whether the resident currently attends day care, the days and hours, and who is responsible for any cost.

If a resident or representative asks to start day care, the Assisted Living Manager or delegating nurse reviews the request with the resident, confirms the resident's wishes, and updates the service plan to reflect the day care schedule (ADM-04).

For Medicaid waiver residents, the Assisted Living Manager notifies the resident's case manager before attendance starts or stops, so the case manager can confirm how it relates to the waiver service authorization and rate (COMAR 10.09.54.13; GOV-06).

The Assisted Living Manager obtains the resident's written consent to share information with the day care, consistent with RR-07, and records the day care's name, address, phone number and the person to contact.

The delegating nurse and the day care's nurse agree in writing on who gives which medications. Medications are given by only one program at a time. Any medication that must be given during day care hours is sent in its labeled container with written instructions, and the receipt and return are recorded (HLT-01, HLT-02).

Staff complete a day care coordination sheet for each attendance day. It lists the resident's medications given before leaving, special diet or care needs, and any change in condition, and it is reviewed and returned with notes from the day care at the end of the day.
Staff review the returned sheet on the resident's return, record any new orders, and report any change in condition or incident at the day care to the delegating nurse (HLT-04).

The Assisted Living Manager arranges transportation to and from the day care with the day care, a family member or the program's own vehicle under DL-04, and the resident is signed out and in using the tracking system.

The Assisted Living Manager confirms meals and snacks for days the resident is away so that the resident does not miss a meal, and confirms any therapeutic diet orders are shared with the day care (DL-01).
If a resident is absent from the program on a day care day, staff confirm the resident's arrival with the day care when expected and follow SAF-03 if the resident cannot be found.
A resident may stop attending at any time. Staff record the resident's decision, update the service plan and tell the resident's case manager if the resident is a waiver participant.

At each six-month service plan review, the delegating nurse and Assisted Living Manager review with the resident and representative whether day care attendance continues to meet the resident's needs and wishes (COMAR 10.07.14.28).

responsibilities.duty: Discloses the policy in the resident agreement, protects voluntary attendance, coordinates with the day care and the waiver case manager, and arranges transportation.
Coordinates medications and nursing information with the day care, reviews returned coordination sheets and updates the service plan.
Complete and review coordination sheets, send and receive medications and belongings, and sign residents out and in.
Decide whether to attend, sign consent to share information, and tell the program about schedule changes.

documentation: Resident agreement disclosure of the adult medical day care policy
Written consent to share information with the day care
Day care schedule recorded in the service plan
Day care coordination sheets
Medication coordination agreement with the day care
Notice to waiver case manager, if applicable
Tracking system entries

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Staffing Levels and Supervision
policies.applies_to: All shifts and all staff; Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager, delegating nurse and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] has enough qualified, supervised staff on duty at all times to meet the scheduled and unscheduled needs of every resident, 24 hours a day.
policies.policy: Maryland sets no numeric staff-to-resident ratio for assisted living. [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written staffing plan based on the assessed needs of its residents, covering scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day (COMAR 10.07.14.14). A staff member is present in the building whenever a resident is in the building or is expected back. When the Resident Assessment Tool indicates that a resident needs it, [AGENCY NAME] provides awake overnight staff. Electronic monitoring may be waived by OHCQ, but not for an Alzheimer's special care unit. Dated staffing schedules are kept on site for 18 months. On-site nursing is provided when ordered. As a Medicaid Community Options Waiver provider, [AGENCY NAME] keeps at least 1 staff member for every 8 residents in the daytime (COMAR 10.09.54.05). A delegating nurse provides clinical oversight as required by COMAR 10.07.14.21.

definitions.definition: The written plan that states the number, type and qualifications of staff on each shift, based on the needs of residents.
A staff member who is awake and on duty throughout the overnight shift, required when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it.
For this policy, the hours of [DAYTIME HOURS], during which the waiver minimum of 1 staff per 8 residents applies.
The registered nurse who has completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course and signed an agreement with the program to delegate and oversee nursing tasks.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager writes a staffing plan before the program opens and updates it whenever the census, the mix of resident needs or the building changes, and at least annually. The plan states the number and type of staff for each shift, the tasks covered, and the on-call arrangements.

The plan is built from the Resident Assessment Tool and nursing assessments for each resident (ADM-03). It accounts for both scheduled needs, such as medication passes, meals, bathing and activities, and unscheduled needs, such as falls, toileting, behaviors, and calls for help.

Each time a resident is admitted, reassessed or has a significant change in condition, the Assisted Living Manager and delegating nurse review whether the staffing plan still meets residents' needs and change it if not, and record the review.

The Assisted Living Manager posts a dated schedule that names each staff member on each shift, including the alternate manager and the staff on call. Changes are written on the schedule the day they happen.
A staff member is always present in the building whenever any resident is present or is expected back, including when residents are out and are due to return.

For waiver participation, the schedule shows at least 1 staff member for every 8 residents during the daytime hours. The Assisted Living Manager checks the ratio at each schedule posting and daily against the census (COMAR 10.09.54.05).

If any resident's Resident Assessment Tool triggers the need for awake overnight staff, the Assisted Living Manager schedules at least one awake staff member for every overnight shift while that resident lives in the program, and records the trigger in the plan.

If the program has electronic monitoring in place of awake overnight staff, the Assisted Living Manager keeps OHCQ's written waiver on file. No waiver applies in an Alzheimer's special care unit, which always meets the overnight staffing requirement in its approved plan (HLT-05).
Staff schedules are kept on site, dated and complete with actual hours worked, for 18 months and are available to OHCQ surveyors on request.

The Assisted Living Manager arranges coverage for absences, using relief staff who meet the training and screening requirements of STF-02 and STF-03. No shift is left below the staffing plan. If a call-out creates a gap, the manager or alternate manager is called at once and fills it, and the gap is recorded.

The delegating nurse's signed agreement with [AGENCY NAME] is on file. The delegating nurse observes each resident on site at least every 45 days, is on call at all times (or an alternate nurse is), and reviews the manager's assessments (COMAR 10.07.14.21; HLT-03).

If a resident's physician orders on-site nursing, the Assisted Living Manager arranges it in writing and adds it to the staffing plan before it is needed. [AGENCY NAME] does not otherwise keep a nurse on site on every shift.

A named supervisor is on duty or on call for each shift. The Assisted Living Manager or alternate manager supervises direct care staff, observes care at least [FREQUENCY], and documents corrections and coaching in the personnel record (STF-05).

Staff may tell the Assisted Living Manager at any time that staffing is not enough. The manager reviews each concern within 1 business day and records the outcome. Staffing concerns, incidents linked to staffing and complaints are reported to the quality assurance review (GOV-04).
The Assisted Living Manager reviews the staffing plan with the governing body at least annually (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Writes and updates the staffing plan, schedules staff, checks ratios, keeps schedules for 18 months, and supervises staff.
Assumes the manager's staffing and supervision duties when the manager is absent.
Provides clinical oversight, observes each resident at least every 45 days, is on call, and advises on staffing needs from assessments.
Approves and provides resources for the staffing plan.
Report as scheduled, tell the manager when they cannot, and report staffing concerns.

documentation: Written staffing plan with annual review
Dated daily and weekly staffing schedules kept on site for 18 months
Record of staffing review after each admission, reassessment or significant change
Delegating nurse agreement
OHCQ waiver of electronic monitoring, if any
Coverage and call-out log
Supervision notes

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, the Assisted Living Manager and alternate manager, owners and, where the application requires it, household members
policies.purpose: To make sure no person who has a harmful criminal history or who is excluded from federal health care programs is hired, and that required background checks and registry checks are completed and documented before a person works with residents.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] completes a criminal history records check on each person who will work for the program within 30 calendar days before the start of employment (COMAR 10.07.14.19). The check is performed under Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901 and is documented in the personnel file (COMAR 10.07.14.20). The program also checks the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities before hire (COMAR 10.07.14.20; 42 USC 1320a-7). Checks also cover owners, managers and household members as the OHCQ application requires. [AGENCY NAME] does not knowingly employ any individual with a harmful criminal history (COMAR 10.07.14.37). A person whose checks are not complete does not work with residents.

definitions.definition: A State and federal fingerprint-based check of a person's criminal record, completed under HG §19-1901 and recorded in the personnel file.
The List of Excluded Individuals/Entities kept by the HHS Office of Inspector General. Persons on it are barred from federal health care programs under 42 USC 1320a-7.
A criminal history that makes a person unsuitable to work with vulnerable adults under COMAR 10.07.14.37 and HG §19-1901.
An adult who lives in a home where an assisted living program operates and for whom the OHCQ application requires a background check.

procedures: Before making an offer of employment, the Assisted Living Manager tells each applicant in writing that employment depends on a satisfactory criminal history records check and OIG exclusion check, and that false information is grounds for refusal or termination.

The Assisted Living Manager or [HR DESIGNEE] starts the criminal history records check through the State process for assisted living staff, and records the date requested and the applicant's authorization in the personnel file. The check is dated no earlier than 30 calendar days before the employee's start date (COMAR 10.07.14.19).

Before the start date, the manager checks the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities for the applicant, prints or saves a dated screenshot of the result, and places it in the personnel file (COMAR 10.07.14.20). An applicant listed as excluded is not hired.

The Assisted Living Manager reviews the criminal history result. If the result shows a conviction or other record that may be harmful, the manager does not allow the person to work with residents until the review is finished, and consults [LEGAL COUNSEL] or OHCQ as needed.

The program does not knowingly employ any individual with a harmful criminal history. If the manager decides a record is harmful under COMAR 10.07.14.37 and HG §19-1901, the offer is withdrawn and the decision is documented without placing details in unrelated records.

The program does not let any person work or volunteer in direct care, or with resident funds, medications or records, until the criminal history check and the OIG check are on file and satisfactory. A new hire who has not yet received results is not left alone with residents and does not work unsupervised.

The Assisted Living Manager verifies professional licenses and certifications that a position requires, such as a nursing license or Board of Nursing medication technician certification, with the issuing board, and records the date, result and expiration date in the personnel file (STF-05).

The Assisted Living Manager arranges the criminal history records check for owners, the manager, the alternate manager and any household member, as the OHCQ application requires, before the application is filed, and when a new owner, manager or household member joins later. Results are kept in a confidential file.

Contractors and temporary staff, including agency or relief staff, who work with residents must meet the same checks. The program obtains written proof from the staffing agency, or does its own checks, before the person works.

The program checks the OIG exclusion list again for all employees and contractors at least monthly and records the date. Any match is reported at once to the Assisted Living Manager, the person is removed from duty, and the program follows GOV-05 for any required report or repayment.

Employees must tell the Assisted Living Manager within 2 business days if they are arrested, charged with or convicted of a crime, or are excluded or sanctioned by a licensing board or health care program. The manager reviews the report and acts as this policy requires.

Criminal history and exclusion records are kept in the personnel file or in a restricted file that only the Assisted Living Manager, alternate manager and governing body representative can open, and are kept as required by STF-05.
Results are not shared with residents, other employees or unrelated third parties. They are available to OHCQ surveyors on request.

The Assisted Living Manager audits all personnel files at least annually for complete, timely background check and OIG documentation and reports gaps to the governing body and the quality assurance review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Starts checks, reviews results, checks the OIG list before hire and monthly, bars unscreened individuals from resident contact, and keeps the records.
Ensures owners and the manager are screened, and reviews decisions involving the manager or alternate manager.
Give accurate information, authorize checks and report arrests, convictions and exclusions.
Carries out these duties when the manager is absent, and cannot review their own check.

documentation: Signed authorization and notice to applicant
Criminal history records check result and date, in the personnel file
Dated OIG exclusion list result before hire and each monthly check
License and certification verification
Checks for owners, managers and household members
Annual personnel file audit
Employee self-reports of arrests, charges, convictions or exclusions

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, the Assisted Living Manager, the alternate manager and the delegating nurse of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who works at [AGENCY NAME] is old enough, qualified, oriented and trained before working with residents. It also keeps staff trained every year, with proof of training that is ready for OHCQ review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires, orients and trains staff as required by COMAR 10.07.14.19 (Other Staff - Qualifications), COMAR 10.07.14.47 (Emergency Preparedness) and COMAR 10.07.14.21 (Delegating Nurse). Direct-care staff are at least 18 years old. A person aged 16 or 17 may be used in direct care only if the person is a certified nursing assistant (CNA) or is enrolled in CNA training. No employee works alone with residents until the pre-employment checks, orientation and competency steps in this policy are complete. Each employee receives initial and annual training, and the program keeps proof of that training for every employee, including relief staff. This policy meets the training and qualification requirements of COMAR 10.07.14.19 and the emergency orientation and drill requirements of COMAR 10.07.14.47.

definitions.definition: Employees who give residents hands-on personal care, medication assistance or supervision.
Employees or agency personnel who fill in for regular staff. They meet the same qualification, background check, health and training requirements as regular staff.

The registered nurse (RN) who has a signed agreement with the program and has completed the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course. The RN delegates and oversees personal care tasks, as described in COMAR 10.07.14.21.
Demonstrated ability to perform a personal care task safely and correctly, confirmed by the delegating nurse.

definitions.term: Cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training
definitions.definition: The role-based training that COMAR 10.07.14.19 requires on dementia and other cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health.

procedures: Before making an offer, the Assisted Living Manager confirms the applicant meets the minimum age: 18 or older for direct care, or 16 to 17 only if the applicant is a CNA or in CNA training. The manager notes the age check and CNA status on the hiring checklist.
The manager confirms the applicant's licensure or certification, where one is required for the position (for example CNA or certified medication technician), and files a copy.

The manager confirms that the criminal history records check was completed within the 30 calendar days before the start of employment, as COMAR 10.07.14.19 requires. If the check is not complete or is older than 30 calendar days, the applicant does not start. See STF-02.

The manager confirms that TB screening and evidence of MMR and varicella immunity are on file before the first shift, and that the OIG exclusion list check was done before hire. See STF-04 and STF-05.

On or before the first day, the manager gives the employee a job description and the policies on abuse and neglect reporting, resident rights and confidentiality. The employee signs and dates a receipt.

Within 24 hours of the start date, and before the employee works alone, the manager or designee orients the employee to the emergency preparedness plan as required by COMAR 10.07.14.47. This covers evacuation routes, fire alarm and extinguisher locations, shelter-in-place, the tracking system and the medical fact sheets. The employee signs the orientation record.

Before the employee works alone, the manager provides orientation on resident rights, abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting, infection control, the resident's service plan and record, medication policies as they apply to the role, and elopement and incident procedures.

Staff who are not CNAs and who provide personal care must show competence to the delegating nurse before working alone. Until the delegating nurse signs the competency checklist, the employee works accompanied by a qualified staff member for no more than 10 days. If competency is not shown within that period, the employee does not give personal care alone.
The delegating nurse observes each task on the competency checklist, signs and dates the results, and records any retraining needed. The manager files the checklist in the personnel record.

The manager schedules each employee for the initial cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training. The program assigns the 6-hour or 2-hour initial course, and later the 2-hour or 1-hour annual course, that COMAR 10.07.14.19 requires for the employee's role. The manager and delegating nurse confirm each assignment.
The manager makes sure first aid training is current for staff, repeated every 2 years, and that CPR-trained staff are scheduled so that CPR-trained coverage is available 24 hours a day.

Every year each employee completes training in fire and life safety, infection control, food safety and the disaster plans. Staff are also trained in the use of fire extinguishers, initially and annually, as COMAR 10.07.14.47 requires.

Staff take part in quarterly fire drills on all shifts and semiannual disaster drills on all shifts. The manager records attendance on the drill record and keeps those records for 2 years. See SAF-05 and SAF-06.
For every training session, the trainer or manager keeps proof showing the date, the content or outline, the trainer's name and qualifications, and the signatures of staff who attended.

The manager keeps a training tracking log with each employee's due dates. At the start of each month the manager reviews the log, notifies employees of upcoming due dates, and schedules make-up sessions within 30 days of a missed session. An employee with overdue required training is not scheduled to work alone until the training is complete.
Relief and agency staff do not work a shift until the manager has verified the same documents as for regular staff and has completed the orientation steps above.
The manager reports training status to the governing body in the quality assurance review. See GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies age, background check, health and licensure documents. Delivers or arranges orientation and training. Keeps the training log and proof of training. Does not allow an employee to work alone until all steps are complete.
Teaches and observes personal care competencies, signs the competency checklist, and reviews the training needs of direct-care staff.
Complete the orientation and training on time, sign the attendance records and tell the manager if a license, certification or health document is about to expire.
Provides time and resources for training and reviews training compliance during quality assurance.

documentation: Hiring checklist showing age, CNA status and licensure verification
Signed orientation records, including the emergency preparedness orientation completed within 24 hours of hire
Delegating nurse competency checklists
Training attendance records with date, content, trainer and signatures
Training tracking log
First aid and CPR certificates
Fire and disaster drill records, kept 2 years

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff and the Assisted Living Manager of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease by requiring tuberculosis (TB) screening and evidence of immunity for all staff. It also keeps employee health information confidential and uses the annual TB risk assessment to guide the program.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires TB screening and evidence of MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) and varicella immunity for all staff, including the Assisted Living Manager and relief staff, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.15 and COMAR 10.07.14.19. The program advises flu and COVID-19 vaccination and documents each employee's decision. The program completes an annual TB risk assessment as part of its quality assurance plan under COMAR 10.07.14.13. Employee health information is kept in a separate confidential file under COMAR 10.07.14.20. The program follows the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101 et seq.) when handling employee health matters.

definitions.definition: The TB test or symptom screening that the program's TB risk assessment and the delegating nurse direct, completed under COMAR 10.07.14.19.
A vaccination record, laboratory result or physician statement showing immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella.
A yearly review of TB risk in the program and its community. It is part of quality assurance and determines how often staff are screened.
A file separate from the general personnel file that holds medical and health information and is accessible only to those with a need to know.

procedures: Before an employee's first shift, the Assisted Living Manager collects written evidence of TB screening and of MMR and varicella immunity. The manager does not schedule an employee for work until this evidence is on file.

If an employee lacks evidence of immunity, the manager refers the employee to the delegating nurse, the employee's health care provider or the local health department for testing or vaccination. The manager follows the delegating nurse's direction on work until immunity is shown, consistent with COMAR 10.07.14.19.

The manager places TB and immunity results in the confidential employee health file, not in the general work file. The personnel file contains only a checklist showing that the requirement was met. See STF-05.
The manager repeats TB screening as the annual TB risk assessment and the delegating nurse direct, and tracks due dates on the health tracking log.
Each year the manager and delegating nurse complete the annual TB risk assessment and attach it to the quality assurance plan. The assessment is reviewed by the governing body. See GOV-04.

At hire, and each fall, the manager offers each employee information on flu and COVID-19 vaccines. The program advises vaccination but does not make it a condition of employment unless the governing body adopts a separate written requirement.

The employee records acceptance, declination or an exemption on the vaccination form. The manager files the form in the confidential health file, as COMAR 10.07.14.20 expects documentation of the advisory.

An employee with symptoms of active TB or of a communicable illness must tell the manager at once and stay away from residents. The manager arranges evaluation and clearance by a health care provider before the employee returns.

If an employee has a confirmed or suspected case of active TB, the manager notifies the delegating nurse and the local health department the same day, follows their instructions, and records residents and staff who may have been exposed.

The manager provides bloodborne pathogen training at hire and yearly, with personal protective equipment, sharps containers and exposure control procedures available as 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires. See SAF-07.

If an employee has an exposure to blood or body fluids, the employee reports it at once. The manager arranges immediate first aid and medical evaluation, and documents the incident in a confidential exposure record.

The manager makes any request for medical information or accommodation only as the Americans with Disabilities Act permits. The program considers reasonable accommodation requests through an interactive process and keeps those records in the confidential health file.

The manager restricts access to the confidential health file to the manager, the delegating nurse and the administrator, and shares information only where law permits. The file is available to OHCQ at survey.
Every quarter the manager reviews the health tracking log for missing or expiring items and corrects gaps within 14 days.
Relief and agency staff meet the same TB and immunity requirements before working a shift. The manager keeps copies or obtains written verification from the staffing agency.

responsibilities.duty: Collects, reviews and files TB and immunity evidence. Keeps the health tracking log. Maintains the confidential employee health file. Completes the annual TB risk assessment with the delegating nurse.
Advises on TB screening frequency, follow-up of positive results and exposure response. Reviews the annual TB risk assessment.
Provide required health documents. Report symptoms of communicable illness and exposures promptly.
Reviews the annual TB risk assessment through quality assurance and decides on any vaccine requirement.

documentation: TB screening results
MMR and varicella immunity evidence
Flu and COVID-19 vaccination advisory, acceptance or declination forms
Annual TB risk assessment in the quality assurance file
Employee health tracking log
Confidential exposure incident records
Checklist in the personnel file showing the health requirements are met

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Personnel files of all employees, relief staff, the Assisted Living Manager and the delegating nurse of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every employee has a complete, current personnel file containing everything COMAR 10.07.14.20 requires, and that the files are ready when OHCQ asks to see them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel file for each employee, including relief staff, as required by COMAR 10.07.14.20 (Personnel Records) and COMAR 10.07.14.19 (Other Staff - Qualifications). Each file contains the criminal history records check (conducted under Md. Code, Health-General §19-1901), TB and immunity evidence, the flu and COVID-19 vaccine advisory, licensure or certification, training records and the OIG exclusion list check. Certified medication technician (CMT) certification is kept in the file of each CMT. Files are complete before an employee works alone and are available to OHCQ at the survey.

definitions.definition: The record for one employee containing the items required by COMAR 10.07.14.20.
The check of an employee's criminal history conducted under Health-General §19-1901 and documented under COMAR 10.07.14.20.
A search of the federal Office of Inspector General list of excluded individuals, completed before hire.
Certification by the Maryland Board of Nursing as a certified medication technician.
Per diem or agency staff who fill in for regular staff.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager opens a personnel file on the date an offer is accepted, using the personnel file checklist for this program.
Before the first shift, the manager confirms the file contains the application and job description, proof of age, and the employee's position and start date.

The manager files the criminal history records check result, showing it was completed within the 30 calendar days before employment, as COMAR 10.07.14.19 requires. Checks are handled under Health-General §19-1901. See STF-02.

The manager runs the OIG exclusion list check before hire, prints or saves the result with the date and the name of the person who ran it, and files it. The manager repeats the check each month and files the result. If the employee appears on the list, the manager does not employ or keeps from duty the employee and notifies the administrator at once.
The manager files evidence of TB screening and MMR and varicella immunity, or a checklist pointing to the confidential health file where the detailed results are held. See STF-04.
The manager files the flu and COVID-19 vaccine advisory form showing the employee was advised and what the employee chose.

The manager files copies of licenses and certifications that apply to the position. For each CMT this includes the Board of Nursing certification, which the manager verifies on the Board's website at hire and at each renewal date.
The manager files copies of first aid and CPR certificates, and the delegating nurse's signed competency checklist where the employee provides personal care without being a CNA.
The manager files proof of orientation and training for each session, showing date, content, trainer and the employee's signature, as COMAR 10.07.14.19 requires. See STF-03.
The manager files any signed policy acknowledgments, performance evaluations, disciplinary actions and the date and reason for separation.
Medical, health and immigration documents are kept in separate confidential files, not with the general file. The personnel file shows only that the requirement was met.
Relief and agency staff have the same file contents. If a staffing agency holds the records, the manager obtains copies or written verification before the first shift and keeps them on site.

Files are stored in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system on the premises. Only the manager, the administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the delegating nurse may open them, and OHCQ surveyors may review them on request.

Each month the manager checks every file against the checklist and the tracking log for expiring licenses, TB, training and certifications. Gaps are corrected within 14 days, and the manager records the correction.
Before each OHCQ survey or license renewal, and at least once a year, the administrator audits a sample of files and reports results to the quality assurance committee. See GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Builds and maintains every personnel file. Runs OIG checks. Verifies licenses and CMT certification. Tracks expiring items. Presents files to OHCQ.
Audits sample files at least yearly. Makes sure no employee works without a complete file.
Signs competency checklists for the personnel file and advises on clinical credentials.
Give accurate documents and renewals before they expire.

documentation: Personnel file checklist for each employee
Criminal history records check result
OIG exclusion list check results (at hire and monthly)
TB and immunity evidence or checklist
Flu and COVID-19 advisory forms
Licenses, CMT certification, CPR and first aid certificates
Training records and delegating nurse competency checklists
Monthly file review log and annual audit report

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, volunteers, contractors, the Assisted Living Manager and the delegating nurse of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect residents from financial exploitation, abuse and undue influence by setting clear rules for staff conduct, and to make sure that suspected abuse is reported within the legal deadline.
policies.policy: Staff of [AGENCY NAME] keep professional boundaries with residents at all times. Staff may not exploit residents financially. They may not take gifts or loans from residents, may not accept a bequest or ask to be named in a resident's will, and may not use a resident's funds or property for any personal purpose. Residents may work for the program only with their consent and with compensation, as COMAR 10.07.14.36 requires. Staff must report suspected abuse, neglect or financial exploitation within the 24-hour window required by COMAR 10.07.14.37. The program may manage a resident's funds only as COMAR 10.07.14.39 allows. Any breach of this policy results in discipline, documented in the personnel file, and may be reported to law enforcement and licensing authorities.

definitions.definition: Improper use of a resident's money, property or assets for the benefit of someone other than the resident, including taking, borrowing or misusing resident funds.
The limit that separates a caregiver's role from personal, financial or social relationships with a resident.
Anything of value given to a staff member by a resident or representative, including money, goods and services.
Any task a resident performs for the program. It is allowed only with the resident's consent and compensation.

procedures: At hire and every year, each employee receives this policy and the abuse, neglect and exploitation policy (SAF-01), and signs an acknowledgment filed in the personnel file.

Staff do not ask for, accept or keep gifts, money, loans or favors from residents, representatives or family members. If a resident insists on giving something, the staff member declines politely, or accepts it only to hand it at once to the manager, who documents it and works with the resident or representative on its return.
Staff do not borrow from or lend money to residents, buy or sell items to residents, or use a resident's property, vehicle, phone, accounts or credit and debit cards.

Staff do not ask a resident to name them in a will, trust, insurance policy or power of attorney, and do not serve as agent, witness or beneficiary for a resident. If a resident raises such a request, the staff member tells the manager.

Staff do not handle a resident's money or valuables except through the program's resident funds procedure in RR-05, which applies only on the resident's or agent's express written request, as COMAR 10.07.14.39 requires. Two staff are involved in any cash transaction, and each transaction is receipted and logged.
Staff do not request, sign or witness a resident's financial documents, or use a resident's identification or personal information, other than as the manager directs for care purposes.

A resident may do work for the program, such as helping in the kitchen or laundry, only if the resident freely agrees, the work is noted in the service plan, and the resident is paid. The manager records the consent, the task and the compensation. A resident is never required to work, and refusing carries no consequence.

Staff do not form romantic or sexual relationships with residents, do not use resident rooms for personal use, and do not socialize with residents outside work in ways that create dependence or favoritism.
Staff do not share personal social media content about residents or post photographs of residents without written consent. See RR-07.
Staff treat residents with dignity, honor the rights in the Resident Bill of Rights (RR-01) and never use threats, coercion or retaliation against a resident who complains.

Any staff member who sees or suspects abuse, neglect or financial exploitation tells the manager immediately and no later than the end of the shift. The manager, or the staff member if the manager is unavailable, then reports within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, and the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services, as COMAR 10.07.14.37 requires. Failure to report within 3 days can bring a penalty of up to $1,000.
The manager begins an investigation promptly, protects the resident, separates the accused staff member from the resident when needed, and documents the investigation on site. See SAF-01.
Staff who report in good faith are protected from retaliation. Retaliation is itself grounds for discipline.
Staff who see a boundary concern, such as gifts offered, unusual requests or a co-worker's behavior, report it to the manager the same day, and the manager records the report.

The manager reviews violations and decides on action, which can include coaching, written warning, suspension or termination. All discipline is documented and signed, and a copy is placed in the personnel file. Staff who commit abuse or exploitation are removed from resident contact at once.
The manager reviews boundary concerns and discipline trends at least quarterly with the administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] as part of quality assurance.

responsibilities.duty: Follow the conduct rules, decline gifts and loans, and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.
Trains staff, receives reports, makes the 24-hour reports, investigates, documents discipline in the personnel file and supervises any resident work arrangement.
Reviews serious breaches, makes sure reports reach all required agencies and decides on termination.
Reports suspected abuse or neglect seen during visits and supports staff training.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgments of this policy
Gift or loan incident notes held by the manager
Resident work consent and compensation records
24-hour reports and investigation records
Disciplinary documents in the personnel file
Quarterly review notes

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All resident records, paper and electronic, kept by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure a complete, accurate and confidential record is kept for each resident, kept for the required time and released or disposed of only as the law permits.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for each resident with the contents listed in COMAR 10.07.14.29. Care notes are written at least weekly and after any event. The delegating nurse reassesses a resident within 48 hours of readmission. The record is kept for 5 years after the resident is discharged. Records are kept confidential and are released and disposed of as the Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act (Md. Code, Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3) permits. The program follows the HIPAA privacy standard on administrative requirements (45 CFR 164.530) for staff training, safeguards and complaints about privacy.

definitions.definition: The complete set of paper and electronic documents about one resident, including the items required by COMAR 10.07.14.29.
A dated and signed entry describing the resident's condition, care given, events and response.
A resident's return to the program after a hospital stay or other absence from which the program accepts the resident back.
The 5 years after discharge during which the record must be kept.

procedures: On or before the admission date, the Assisted Living Manager opens a record for the resident and organizes it under standard sections using the Resident Record Checklist for this program. The checklist is based on the contents required by COMAR 10.07.14.29, and the manager checks it against the regulation each year.

The record includes at least the signed resident agreement and Uniform Disclosure Statement, the Resident Assessment Tool and nursing assessments, the service plan, physician and other health provider orders, medication and treatment records, care notes, incident reports, advance directive and preference documents, and the discharge or transfer documents when they apply. The manager completes any other item the checklist lists for the resident.
Within 30 calendar days of admission the manager makes sure the service plan is filed in the record. See ADM-04 and REC-02.

Staff who give care write a care note at least once a week for every resident, and also on the day of any event, such as a fall, change of condition, medication change, hospital visit, behavior concern, family contact or refusal of care. Each note is dated, timed, signed and legible.
Staff correct errors by drawing a single line, writing the correct information with initials and date, and never by erasing or using correction fluid. Electronic systems keep an audit trail of edits.

When a resident returns from a hospital or other facility, the delegating nurse reassesses the resident within 48 hours of readmission, records the reassessment in the record and updates the service plan as needed. See HLT-04 and ADM-04.
Paper records are kept in a locked cabinet or room. Electronic records require individual passwords and are backed up daily. Staff may see only the information they need to do their jobs.
Records stay on the premises, or are available on the premises to OHCQ on request. Records are not removed except in an emergency, for transfer with the resident or as the law allows.

The manager releases information only as the Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act (Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3) permits, such as with the resident's or representative's written authorization or to OHCQ or other authorities with lawful access. The manager records every release in a disclosure log.

Residents and their representatives may ask to see or get a copy of the record. The manager arranges review within a reasonable time, explains entries on request, and documents the access in the log. See RR-07.
Staff receive training at hire and every year on record confidentiality and HIPAA safeguards. Privacy complaints are handled under RR-02 and RR-07, as 45 CFR 164.530 provides.
When a resident is discharged or dies, the manager completes the record within 30 days, marks the discharge date on the cover and moves the record to closed storage.

The manager keeps each record for 5 years after the discharge date, and longer if a legal hold, investigation or dispute is pending. The manager keeps an index of closed records showing the discharge date and the destruction date.

After the retention period ends, and after the administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] approves in writing, records are destroyed in a way that makes them unreadable, such as cross-cut shredding or certified electronic deletion, as Health-General Title 4, Subtitle 3 provides. The manager records the date, method and the person who destroyed them.

If the program closes or changes ownership, the administrator notifies OHCQ and arranges for safe custody of records as the law allows, so that residents and former residents can get access for the remaining retention period. See GOV-02.
The manager audits at least five resident records every quarter for completeness, timeliness and legibility, and reports results to the quality assurance committee. See GOV-04.

Documents nursing assessments and the 48-hour readmission reassessment, and reviews nursing entries.
Write timely, accurate weekly and event care notes, and protect the confidentiality of records.
Approves record destruction and makes sure records are secure.

policies.title: Documentation Policies and Procedures (Resident Condition and Preferences)
policies.applies_to: All staff of [AGENCY NAME] who observe, assess, care for or document information about residents
policies.purpose: To make sure all pertinent information about each resident's condition and preferences is documented and passed on to the staff who need it, so that care matches the resident's needs and wishes.
policies.policy: This policy meets OHCQ Application, Step Three, item 5(f) — Documentation Policies and Procedures to ensure all pertinent information relating to a resident's condition and preferences is documented and communicated. [AGENCY NAME] documents each resident's condition and preferences in the Resident Assessment Tool and the service plan, and communicates any change to the staff who give care. The Resident Assessment Tool is completed within 30 days before admission and reviewed every 6 months (COMAR 10.07.14.22). The service plan is completed within 30 calendar days of admission, reviewed every 6 months, and fully reassessed at least yearly and within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization (COMAR 10.07.14.28). Care notes are written at least weekly and on events (COMAR 10.07.14.29). Incident reports are completed within 24 hours of knowledge (COMAR 10.07.14.33). The delegating nurse documents findings at the 45-day visit and at the 6-month reviews. The resident and the resident's representative are invited to service plan meetings.

definitions.definition: The assessment of the resident's physical, cognitive, behavioral, medication and psychosocial needs and preferences that the program completes before admission and reviews every 6 months.
The written plan of services based on the Resident Assessment Tool and the nursing assessment, including the resident's preferences and special care needs.
A major change in the resident's physical or mental condition that is expected to last or that affects the services needed, such as a decline in function, new behaviors or a change in medical status.
A hospital stay that is not a planned or regular admission, including emergency admissions.
A dated, timed and signed entry about the resident's condition, care and any event.
The resident's choices about daily routine, food, activities, personal care, privacy, visitors, spiritual life and end-of-life care.

procedures: The Assisted Living Manager completes the Resident Assessment Tool, including the resident's choices and preferences, within the 30 days before admission, with the resident, the representative and the health provider information. See ADM-03.

The delegating nurse reviews the manager's assessment and completes the nursing assessment, and records any nursing orders and special care needs such as falls, pressure ulcers, diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, catheter, ostomy, mental illness and behaviors.

Within 30 calendar days of admission, the manager and delegating nurse complete the service plan, based on the Resident Assessment Tool and the nursing assessment. It states the services to be given, who gives them, how often and the resident's preferences about how they are given. See ADM-04.

The manager invites the resident and representative to every service plan meeting, at a time and place that suits them, and records who attended, who was invited and any views or objections raised. If they cannot attend, the manager offers another way for them to take part.

The manager reviews the Resident Assessment Tool and the service plan with the delegating nurse at least every 6 months, and again whenever the resident's condition or preferences change. Changes are dated and signed.

Within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, the delegating nurse and manager complete a full reassessment and update the service plan. A full reassessment is also done at least once a year.

The delegating nurse visits each resident on site at least every 45 days. The nurse writes a dated, signed note on the resident's condition, any change, the effectiveness of the plan and any orders or training given to staff, and the note is filed in the record.

Staff write a care note for each resident at least once a week, and also on the same shift as any event, such as a fall, injury, behavior, new symptom, refusal of care or medication, family contact or change in eating, sleep or mood. Notes describe what staff saw and did, not just conclusions.
Staff record the resident's stated preferences and refusals in the care note and tell the manager when a preference cannot be met, so that the service plan can be reviewed.

Staff complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowing about the incident, using the program's incident form. The report includes the content COMAR 10.07.14.33 requires and shows who was notified. Reports are kept available on the premises for OHCQ. See SAF-02.

At each shift change, the outgoing lead staff member gives a verbal and written report to the incoming staff on every resident's condition changes, new orders, incidents, appointments, refusals and special preferences. The report is recorded in the shift communication log.

When the service plan or an order changes, the manager updates the staff care instructions (care card or equivalent) the same day, reviews the change with every shift within 72 hours, and records who was told and when.

The manager notifies the resident's representative, physician or other health provider when the resident's condition changes, as the policy on change of condition requires. The call, the person contacted and the response are recorded in a care note. See HLT-04.
Staff sign and date every entry. Late entries are labeled as late and show the date written and the date of the event. Staff do not alter or remove prior entries.

The manager reviews at least five records each month for timely weekly notes, 6-month reviews, 45-day nurse notes and incident reports filed within 24 hours. The manager corrects gaps within 7 days and reports the findings to the quality assurance committee. See GOV-04.
Staff learn this policy at orientation and every year, and the manager keeps the training record. See STF-03.

Completes nursing assessments, reassesses within 48 hours of a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, visits each resident at least every 45 days and documents findings and orders.
Write accurate weekly and event care notes, document preferences and refusals, report changes and complete incident reports within 24 hours.
Share information about preferences and needs, and take part in service plan meetings.
