policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Owner/governing body, Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager, all employees who witness, receive or learn of a reportable event, and the staff member who maintains the report calendar and files
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] makes every report it owes the State of Maryland on time, to the right agency and in writing: incident reports and death notifications, abuse, neglect and exploitation reports, license-change notices to the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), code-citation reports, Uniform Disclosure Statement amendments, and advance notice of ownership change, relocation or closure.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will make every report required of an assisted living program under COMAR 10.07.14 within the required time, using the required method and agency. The deadlines are fixed. (1) Incident reports are completed within 24 hours of staff knowledge of the event (C31). (2) Abuse, neglect and financial exploitation are reported within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services, and the Assisted Living Manager (C35). (3) A resident death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns, or any injury incurred at the program is reported to OHCQ within 24 hours (C31). (4) Changes to the information in the license application are reported to OHCQ immediately. Code citations are reported within 7 days. OHCQ approval is obtained before beds are added or the level of care is raised (C8). (5) The Uniform Disclosure Statement is amended and filed within 30 days of a service change (C10). (6) At least 60 days' notice is given to OHCQ of an ownership change, relocation or closure for programs with 49 or fewer beds (C8). Any employee may make a required report. No one may delay, discourage, screen or retaliate against a report. If a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the report is still made within the deadline. A report is never held back to complete an investigation. Reports are kept on site and are available to OHCQ. Under C35, failure to report abuse, neglect or exploitation within 3 days can bring a penalty of up to $1,000, so [AGENCY NAME] treats the 24-hour deadline as the standard. This policy has no checklist items assigned to it; it supports the policies listed under Related.

definitions.definition: The Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality, Assisted Living Team, which licenses and surveys assisted living programs. Phone (410) 402-8217 or (800) 492-6005; fax (410) 402-8211.
The written report of an accident, injury, death, elopement, medication error or other significant event involving a resident, completed within 24 hours of knowledge.
Any suspected or known abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a resident, whoever is alleged to be responsible. A report is made on reasonable suspicion; proof is not required.
Any change to information given to OHCQ in the license application, for example ownership or governing body, Assisted Living Manager, contact information, or the services offered.
A written finding that the program did not comply with a requirement, issued after an OHCQ survey or investigation.
The OHCQ form that tells the public what services, fees and policies the program offers.
The time at which any employee first sees, is told of, or reasonably suspects the event. The 24-hour clock starts then, not when management hears of it.

procedures: Any employee who sees, hears of or suspects a resident injury, death, elopement, medication error, abuse, neglect or exploitation tells the shift supervisor right away. If the supervisor is unavailable or involved, the employee goes directly to the Assisted Living Manager or Alternate Manager. Any employee may report directly to the agencies listed in step 5.
First, staff protect the resident and obtain emergency care (see HLT-04 and SAF-01). Reporting never delays care or protection.

The employee with first-hand knowledge completes the agency incident report form before the end of the shift and in any case within 24 hours of knowledge (C31). The form records the resident, date, time and place, what happened, witnesses, injuries or harm, immediate action taken, and the people notified.

The shift supervisor gives the incident report to the Assisted Living Manager (or Alternate Manager) the same day. The manager reviews it for completeness and decides whether any other report in this policy is also triggered.

For suspected or known abuse, neglect or financial exploitation, the Assisted Living Manager or designee makes a report within 24 hours to each of: law enforcement; OHCQ; the Ombudsman or area agency on aging; and the local Department of Human Services/Adult Protective Services. The Assisted Living Manager is also informed within 24 hours (C35). Staff record the agency, name of the person contacted, date and time, and any report number on the Report Tracking Log.

If the person alleged to be responsible is the Assisted Living Manager, staff report directly to the agencies in step 5 and to the owner/governing body. The Alternate Manager or owner takes over the response.

If a resident dies and the death resulted from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns, or any injury incurred at the program, the Assisted Living Manager notifies OHCQ within 24 hours of the death by phone and in writing (C31). A copy of the incident report is placed in the file for that event. See also HLT-09.

The manager makes the other notifications the incident report form requires (for example, the resident's representative and physician, and any agency listed on the form). Each notification is recorded on the incident report with date, time and name.

The Assisted Living Manager starts an on-site investigation the same day for any abuse, neglect or exploitation allegation and documents the findings and action taken. The investigation file stays on site (C35). Reporting is not postponed to wait for investigation results.
The Assisted Living Manager keeps all incident reports on the premises where OHCQ can see them on request (C31). Copies are filed per REC-01.

The Administrator notifies OHCQ immediately in writing of any change to the information in the license application (C8). Examples are a change of Assisted Living Manager, owner, governing body, mailing address or phone, or services. A copy of the notice and OHCQ's reply are kept in the licensure file (GOV-02).

Before adding beds or raising the level of care (Level 1, 2 or 3), the Administrator submits the request to OHCQ and waits for OHCQ's written approval. No bed is occupied and no resident is admitted at a higher level before approval (C8).

When [AGENCY NAME] receives a code citation, the Administrator reports it to OHCQ within 7 days as C8 requires. The Administrator dates the report, logs it, and sends the plan of correction to the QA committee (GOV-04).

When [AGENCY NAME] plans an ownership change, relocation or closure, the Administrator gives OHCQ written notice at least 60 days beforehand. For a program with more than 49 beds, the Administrator confirms the notice period with OHCQ before taking any step (C8). Notice to residents and representatives follows RR-04 and ADM-08.

The Administrator confirms each year that [AGENCY NAME] is in good standing with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). SDAT good standing is required as a condition of licensure (C8, §H). The Administrator files any annual report SDAT requires and keeps proof of good standing in the licensure file.

Whenever a service, fee or policy described in the Uniform Disclosure Statement changes, the Administrator completes an amended statement on the OHCQ form and files it within 30 days of the service change (C10). The Administrator then replaces the old statement in marketing materials and at the front desk.
The Administrator makes sure the current Uniform Disclosure Statement is given free of charge to anyone who asks and is included in marketing materials (C10). See RR-04.

The Assisted Living Manager reviews the Report Tracking Log each week. Any report without a recorded date, time and confirmation is followed up that day. A late or missed report is documented, reported to the Administrator the same day and made at once, and the cause goes to the QA committee.

The QA committee reviews the Report Tracking Log at least quarterly for timeliness, repeat events, and trends, and recommends corrective actions (GOV-04). Staff are retrained on this policy at orientation and at least yearly (STF-03).

Posted reporting signs, including how to report abuse, neglect or exploitation, are kept visible to residents, visitors and staff. The Assisted Living Manager checks the signs monthly and replaces any missing or outdated sign (C35).

responsibilities.duty: Report any known or suspected reportable event to the supervisor or manager immediately. Complete incident reports within 24 hours. Never delay or hold back a report, and never retaliate against a person who reports.
Ensure resident safety, confirm incident reports are complete, and pass reports to the Assisted Living Manager the same day.

Make or direct the 24-hour abuse, neglect and exploitation reports and OHCQ death notifications. Conduct on-site investigations. Maintain the Report Tracking Log. Keep incident reports on premises. Check posted signs monthly.

Make license-change, bed or level approval, citation, ownership, relocation and closure notices to OHCQ on time. Keep SDAT good standing. Amend and file the Uniform Disclosure Statement within 30 days of a service change. Ensure funds and staff time for compliance.
Receive reports in which the manager is involved. Review report timeliness in QA results. Ensure the Administrator has authority and resources to meet every deadline.
Review reports quarterly for timeliness, trends and corrective action; track late or missed reports to resolution.

official.notes:
The packet has no separate policy-checklist form. The policy list is the Step Three, item 5(a)-(l) list, plus the item 6 menu cycle. Sub-items are lettered a-l in the document, so IDs are written as 'Step Three, 5a' and so on.

Submission: Step One is typed (handwritten applications are returned) and is submitted through OHCQ's 'Submit a License Application' link. There is no application fee. Do not start Step Two until OHCQ says Step One is complete and reviewed. Step Two documents are sent after that. The policies and procedures are not uploaded with Step One. The surveyor reviews them on site in Step Three, after OHCQ approves Steps One and Two, and OHCQ says the review 'will include, but is not limited to' the listed documents. Keep all of them in the manual and ready at the facility. Organize the manual in the document's own order: 5a through 5l, then the 4-week menu cycle with the dietitian or nutritionist's written adequacy statement.

If the survey finds deficiencies, the program gets a Statement of Deficiencies and has 10 business days to submit a Plan of Correction. An incomplete application is administratively closed after 180 days.

Related items in the packet that are not on the policy list:
- The Resident Agreement (Step Two, item 6) is a sample template on the OHCQ website.
- The Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form (Step One, attachment 5) applies only if the program will operate such a unit, and it needs OHCQ written approval first.
- The Uniform Disclosure Statement (Step Two, item 5) is also a form on the OHCQ website.

Outside this packet, COMAR 10.07.14 has other substantive requirements, such as medication management (.31), emergency preparedness (.47) and staffing (.14). I did not list them because they are not in the OHCQ policy list. COMAR .47 requires the emergency plan to include an Emergency Preparedness Packet meeting C(2)-(11), according to OHCQ's FAQ. I did not retrieve the text of .47 itself. OHCQ's FAQ also says it created an informational compliance checklist that surveyors will provide during inspections, but I did not locate that checklist.
